title: ServSafe Food Protection Manager Certification Exam Prep

questions.question: Which THREE of the following are part of a manager's role in a HACCP system?
answers: Developing the HACCP plan.
Training the employees on the HACCP plan.
Monitoring the critical control points (CCPs).
Cooking the food.
Washing the dishes.
Taking out the garbage.
feedbacks: Correct: The manager is responsible for creating the HACCP plan.
Correct: The employees must be trained on how to follow the plan.
Correct: The manager must ensure that the CCPs are being monitored.
Incorrect: The manager may or may not be involved in cooking.
Incorrect: The manager may delegate this task to other employees.
Incorrect: The manager may delegate this task to other employees.
questions.explanation: The manager plays a key role in a HACCP system. They are responsible for developing the plan, training the employees, and monitoring the CCPs.

questions.question: A restaurant has a problem with ants. Which THREE of the following are things the manager can do to help get rid of the ants?
answers: Clean up spills and crumbs immediately.
Store food in sealed containers.
Work with a licensed pest control operator (PCO).
Spray insecticide on the ants whenever you see them.
Leave out a bowl of sugar water to trap the ants.
Ignore the ants and hope they will go away.
feedbacks: Correct: This removes a food source for the ants.
Correct: This also removes a food source for the ants.
Correct: A PCO can provide expert advice and assistance.
Incorrect: This is not an effective long-term solution.
Incorrect: This will only attract more ants.
Incorrect: The problem will only get worse if it is ignored.
questions.explanation: The best way to get rid of ants is to remove their food source and work with a licensed PCO.

questions.question: Which THREE of the following are examples of a physical hazard?
answers: A piece of bone in a fish fillet.
A metal fragment from a meat grinder.
A hair in a bowl of soup.
Bacteria on a cutting board.
Mold on a piece of bread.
A chemical sanitizer in a glass of iced tea.
feedbacks: Correct: This is a natural, but still physical, hazard.
Correct: This is a foreign object that can cause injury.
Correct: This is a physical contaminant.
Incorrect: Bacteria are a biological hazard.
Incorrect: Mold is a biological hazard.
Incorrect: This is a chemical hazard.
questions.explanation: Physical hazards are foreign objects in food that can cause illness or injury. Bones, metal fragments, and hair are all examples of physical hazards.

questions.question: A restaurant is receiving a shipment of dairy products. Which THREE of the following should the receiving employee check for?
answers: The milk is at a temperature of 41°F or lower.
The yogurt containers are sealed and not leaking.
The cheese has a sell-by" date that has not expired."
The ice cream is at a temperature of 32°F.
The butter has a soft, oily texture.
The sour cream has a layer of water on top.
feedbacks: Correct: This is the required temperature for cold TCS food.
Correct: The packaging should be intact.
Correct: The date on the package should be checked.
Incorrect: Ice cream should be received frozen, not at 32°F.
Incorrect: Butter should be firm.
Incorrect: This can be a sign of spoilage.
questions.explanation: When receiving dairy products, the employee should check the temperature, the packaging, and the date.

questions.question: A food handler is preparing to start their shift. They are not feeling well and have a headache and a runny nose. What should they do?
answers: Take some medicine and go to work.
Call their manager and report their symptoms.
Go to work and see how they feel.
Ask a coworker to cover their shift.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The food handler should not self-medicate and go to work.
Correct: The food handler should always report any symptoms of illness to their manager.
Incorrect: This could put the health of the customers at risk.
Incorrect: The food handler should still report their symptoms to the manager.
questions.explanation: A food handler who is not feeling well should always report their symptoms to their manager. The manager can then decide if the food handler is well enough to work and, if so, what tasks they can safely perform.

questions.question: A restaurant is storing food in a walk-in cooler. Which of the following is the correct way to store a container of raw chicken?
answers: On the top shelf, above a container of cooked rice.
On the bottom shelf, below a container of cooked rice.
On the same shelf as a container of cooked rice, as long as they are in separate containers.
On the floor of the cooler.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Raw chicken should be stored on the bottom shelf.
Correct: This prevents the raw chicken from dripping onto the cooked rice.
Incorrect: They should be on separate shelves.
Incorrect: Food should never be stored on the floor.
questions.explanation: To prevent cross-contamination, raw chicken should be stored on the bottom shelf of the cooler, below any ready-to-eat food.

questions.question: A restaurant is using a three-compartment sink to wash dishes. The water in the first compartment is for washing, the water in the second compartment is for rinsing, and the water in the third compartment is for sanitizing. What is the minimum temperature of the water in the second compartment?
answers: The temperature does not matter.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is the minimum temperature for chemical sanitizing.
Correct: The rinse water should be at least 110°F.
Incorrect: This is the temperature for hot water sanitizing.
Incorrect: The temperature of the rinse water is important for removing any remaining soap.
questions.explanation: The water in the rinse compartment of a three-compartment sink should be at least 110°F to effectively remove any soap residue from the dishes.

questions.question: A food handler is preparing to make a batch of potato salad. They will be using a knife and a cutting board. What should they do before they start?
answers: Wash their hands and put on single-use gloves.
Wipe the knife and cutting board with a dry cloth.
Get out all of the ingredients they will need.
Start chopping the potatoes.
feedbacks: Correct: This is the first step in any food preparation task.
Incorrect: The knife and cutting board must be washed and sanitized.
Incorrect: The first step is to wash hands.
Incorrect: The food handler must wash their hands first.
questions.explanation: The first and most important step in any food preparation task is to wash your hands. This helps to prevent the spread of bacteria.

questions.question: A restaurant is having a problem with cockroaches. The manager has hired a pest control operator (PCO) to help get rid of the cockroaches. What is the most important thing the manager can do to help the PCO?
answers: Give the PCO a key to the restaurant so they can come and go as they please.
Deny the cockroaches food, water, and shelter.
Buy a lot of roach spray and spray it around the restaurant.
Close the restaurant for a few days so the PCO can work.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The PCO should schedule their visits with the manager.
Correct: The PCO can kill the cockroaches, but if the restaurant is still attractive to them, more will come.
Incorrect: The PCO will use their own products and methods.
Incorrect: This may not be necessary.
questions.explanation: The most important thing a manager can do to help a PCO is to make the restaurant as unattractive to pests as possible. This means keeping the restaurant clean and dry, and denying pests food, water, and shelter.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a biological hazard?
answers: A piece of glass in a salad.
A sanitizer solution on a cutting board.
E. coli bacteria in a hamburger patty.
A metal shaving in a can of soup.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is a physical hazard.
Incorrect: This is a chemical hazard.
Correct: E. coli is a type of bacteria that can cause foodborne illness.
Incorrect: This is a physical hazard.
questions.explanation: Biological hazards are living organisms, such as bacteria, viruses, parasites, and fungi, that can cause foodborne illness. E. coli is a well-known example of a biological hazard.

questions.question: A restaurant is holding a catered event. The food will be transported in a van to the event site. Which of the following is the most important consideration for transporting the food safely?
answers: The van should be clean and free of pests.
The van should have a good sound system.
The van should be able to go fast to get the food to the event quickly.
The van should have a lot of windows to let in light.
feedbacks: Correct: The food should be transported in a clean and sanitary environment.
Incorrect: This is not a food safety consideration.
Incorrect: Speed is not as important as safety.
Incorrect: This is not a food safety consideration.
questions.explanation: The van used to transport food should be clean and free of pests to prevent the food from becoming contaminated.

questions.question: A restaurant has a new employee who has never worked in a food service establishment before. What is the most important thing the manager should do to train this employee in food safety?
answers: Give the employee a copy of the food code and tell them to read it.
Train the employee on the specific food safety procedures for their job.
Have the employee watch a food safety video.
Assume that the employee will learn about food safety from their coworkers.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is not an effective way to train a new employee.
Correct: The training should be tailored to the employee's specific job duties.
Incorrect: While a video can be a part of the training, it is not enough on its own.
Incorrect: The manager is responsible for ensuring that all employees are properly trained.
questions.explanation: The most effective way to train a new employee in food safety is to provide them with training that is specific to their job duties. This will ensure that they know how to perform their job safely.

questions.question: A food handler is preparing to work with a food that is a known allergen. What is the most important thing they can do to prevent cross-contact?
answers: Wear a mask.
Wash their hands and change their gloves.
Use a separate cutting board.
Cook the food to a high temperature.
feedbacks: Incorrect: A mask will not prevent cross-contact.
Correct: This is the first and most important step in preventing cross-contact.
Incorrect: While a good practice, washing hands and changing gloves is more important.
Incorrect: Cooking does not destroy allergens.
questions.explanation: The most important thing a food handler can do to prevent cross-contact is to wash their hands and change their gloves before handling an allergen-free food.

questions.question: Which of the following is a requirement for a food thermometer?
answers: It must be digital.
It must be accurate to within +/- 2°F.
It must be able to be calibrated.
It must have a long probe.
feedbacks: Incorrect: A dial thermometer is also acceptable.
Correct: A food thermometer must be accurate to within +/- 2°F.
Incorrect: While it is a good idea to have a thermometer that can be calibrated, it is not a requirement.
Incorrect: The length of the probe depends on the type of food being measured.
questions.explanation: A food thermometer must be accurate to within +/- 2°F to ensure that food is being cooked to the proper temperature.

questions.question: A restaurant has a policy that all TCS food must be cooled from 135°F to 41°F or lower in six hours. A food handler is cooling a pot of soup. After two hours, the soup is at 80°F. What should the food handler do?
answers: Continue to cool the soup, as long as it reaches 41°F in the next four hours.
Reheat the soup to 165°F and then start the cooling process over again.
Discard the soup.
Put the soup in the freezer to cool it down more quickly.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The soup did not cool to 70°F within the first two hours.
Correct: The soup did not meet the first stage of the cooling process, so it must be reheated and cooled again.
Incorrect: The soup can be saved if it is reheated and cooled properly.
Incorrect: This can damage the soup and may not cool it evenly.
questions.explanation: The two-stage cooling method requires that food be cooled from 135°F to 70°F within two hours. If this does not happen, the food must be reheated to 165°F and then cooled again.

questions.question: A restaurant is having a problem with mice. The manager has set some traps, but they are not catching any mice. What is the most likely reason for this?
answers: The traps are in the wrong place.
The traps are not baited with the right food.
The mice are too smart to get caught in the traps.
The restaurant does not have a mouse problem.
feedbacks: Correct: Mice tend to travel along walls, so the traps should be placed along the walls.
Incorrect: While the bait is important, the placement of the traps is more critical.
Incorrect: Mice are not that smart.
Incorrect: If there are signs of mice, then there is a mouse problem.
questions.explanation: The most common reason why mouse traps do not work is that they are not placed in the right location. Mice are creatures of habit and tend to run along the walls, so the traps should be placed in their path.

questions.question: A food handler is preparing to start their shift. They are wearing a clean uniform and have their hair tied back. What is the first thing they should do?
answers: Put on a pair of single-use gloves.
Wash their hands.
Get out the ingredients they will need.
Start working.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The first thing is to wash hands.
Correct: Handwashing is the first and most important step in any food preparation task.
Incorrect: The first thing is to wash hands.
Incorrect: The first thing is to wash hands.
questions.explanation: The first thing a food handler should do before starting their shift is to wash their hands. This helps to prevent the spread of bacteria.

questions.question: A restaurant is receiving a delivery of fresh produce. Which of the following is a sign that the produce should be rejected?
answers: The produce is at a temperature of 45°F.
The produce has signs of mold or rot.
The produce is not in its original packaging.
The produce is from a local farm.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While some produce is a TCS food, most is not.
Correct: This is a sign of spoilage.
Incorrect: This is not a reason to reject the produce.
Incorrect: Local produce is often fresher than produce that has been shipped from far away.
questions.explanation: Fresh produce should be rejected if it has signs of spoilage, such as mold, rot, or insect damage.

questions.question: A restaurant has a new employee who is a vegetarian. The employee is concerned about cross-contamination between meat and vegetables. What is the best way for the manager to address the employee's concerns?
answers: Tell the employee that they should not be working in a restaurant that serves meat.
Provide the employee with a separate cutting board and utensils for vegetables.
Tell the employee to just wash the cutting board and utensils well after they are used for meat.
Tell the employee that they are overreacting.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is not a helpful or supportive response.
Correct: This is the best way to prevent cross-contamination.
Incorrect: Washing is not enough to prevent cross-contamination. The equipment must be washed and sanitized.
Incorrect: The employee's concerns are valid.
questions.explanation: The best way to prevent cross-contamination is to use separate equipment for raw meat and vegetables. This will help to ensure that the vegetarian employee's food is not contaminated with meat.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most important reason for a food handler to wear a hair restraint?
answers: To keep their hair out of their eyes.
To prevent their hair from falling into the food.
To make them look more professional.
To keep them from touching their hair.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While this is a benefit of wearing a hair restraint, it is not the most important reason.
Correct: This is the primary reason for wearing a hair restraint.
Incorrect: While a hair restraint can contribute to a professional appearance, it is not the main reason for wearing one.
Incorrect: While this can be a benefit, the main reason is to prevent hair from contaminating the food.
questions.explanation: The main purpose of a hair restraint is to prevent hair from falling into food, which is a physical contaminant.

questions.question: A restaurant is using a new sanitizer. The label on the sanitizer says that it must have a concentration of 200 ppm. What is the best way for the manager to check the concentration of the sanitizer?
answers: Smell the sanitizer to see if it is strong enough.
Look at the color of the sanitizer to see if it is dark enough.
Use a test strip to measure the concentration of the sanitizer.
Ask the employees if they think the sanitizer is working.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The smell of the sanitizer is not a reliable indicator of its concentration.
Incorrect: The color of the sanitizer is not a reliable indicator of its concentration.
Correct: A test strip is the only accurate way to measure the concentration of a sanitizer.
Incorrect: The employees' opinion is not a reliable measure of the sanitizer's effectiveness.
questions.explanation: A test strip is a small strip of paper that is treated with a chemical that will change color when it comes into contact with a sanitizer. The color of the test strip can then be compared to a chart to determine the concentration of the sanitizer.

questions.question: A restaurant has a policy that all employees must wash their hands for at least 20 seconds. A new employee is not following this policy. What is the best way for the manager to handle this situation?
answers: Fire the employee immediately.
Talk to the employee and explain the importance of the policy.
Write the employee up for not following the policy.
Ignore the situation and hope the employee will start following the policy on their own.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is too harsh for a first offense.
Correct: The manager should first try to educate the employee about the policy.
Incorrect: This may be necessary if the employee continues to not follow the policy, but it is not the first step.
Incorrect: The manager has a responsibility to enforce the food safety policies.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a situation in which an employee is not following a food safety policy is to first talk to the employee and explain the importance of the policy. If the employee continues to not follow the policy, then disciplinary action may be necessary.

questions.question: A restaurant is holding a buffet. A customer tells the manager that the hot food on the buffet is cold. What should the manager do first?
answers: Take the temperature of the food.
Apologize to the customer and offer them a free meal.
Tell the customer that they are wrong and that the food is hot.
Discard all of the food on the buffet.
feedbacks: Correct: The manager needs to verify that the food is at an unsafe temperature.
Incorrect: While this may be a good customer service gesture, the first priority is to address the food safety issue.
Incorrect: This is not a good way to handle a customer complaint.
Incorrect: The manager should first take the temperature of the food to see if it is unsafe.
questions.explanation: The first thing a manager should do when a customer complains that the food on a buffet is cold is to take the temperature of the food. This will allow the manager to determine if the food is in the temperature danger zone and needs to be discarded or reheated.

questions.question: Which of the following is a safe way to store chemicals in a food service establishment?
answers: On the top shelf of a dry storage area, above the food.
In their original containers, with the labels clearly visible.
In unmarked spray bottles, for easy access.
In the same area as the food, to save space.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Chemicals should be stored below and away from food.
Correct: This helps to prevent accidental misuse.
Incorrect: All chemical containers must be clearly labeled.
Incorrect: Chemicals should be stored in a separate area from food.
questions.explanation: Chemicals should be stored in a designated area away from food and food-contact surfaces. They should be kept in their original containers with the labels intact to prevent accidental poisoning.

questions.question: A restaurant has a new manager. The manager wants to implement a food safety program. What is the first thing the manager should do?
answers: Buy a lot of new cleaning supplies.
Train the employees on food safety.
Conduct a self-inspection of the restaurant to identify any potential food safety risks.
Write a new food safety manual for the restaurant.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While cleaning supplies are important, this is not the first step.
Incorrect: The manager should first assess the current situation.
Correct: The manager needs to know what the current food safety risks are before they can develop a plan to address them.
Incorrect: The manager should first conduct a self-inspection.
questions.explanation: The first step in implementing a food safety program is to conduct a self-inspection of the restaurant. This will help the manager to identify any potential food safety risks so that they can be addressed in the food safety plan.

questions.question: A food handler is preparing to work with a food that is a known allergen. They have washed their hands and put on new gloves. What is another important step they should take to prevent cross-contact?
answers: Use a separate cutting board and utensils.
Wipe down the work surface with a sanitizer wipe.
Cook the allergen-free food on the same grill as the other food.
Ask the customer if they are sure they are allergic to the food.
feedbacks: Correct: This is the best way to prevent cross-contact.
Incorrect: Wiping is not enough to remove all allergens. The work surface must be washed and sanitized.
Incorrect: This can cause cross-contact.
Incorrect: The food handler should not question the customer's allergy.
questions.explanation: To prevent cross-contact, it is essential to use separate equipment and work surfaces when preparing an allergen-free meal.

questions.question: A restaurant is using a dial food thermometer. How can the manager check the accuracy of the thermometer?
answers: By placing it in a glass of hot water.
By placing it in a glass of ice water.
By comparing it to another thermometer.
By guessing.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is not an accurate way to check the calibration of a thermometer.
Correct: The thermometer should read 32°F in a glass of ice water. This is the ice-point method of calibration.
Incorrect: The other thermometer may not be accurate.
Incorrect: Guessing is not an accurate way to check the calibration of a thermometer.
questions.explanation: The ice-point method is a simple and accurate way to check the calibration of a food thermometer. To do this, fill a glass with crushed ice and water. Place the thermometer in the glass and wait for the reading to steady. The thermometer should read 32°F.

questions.question: A restaurant has a policy that all TCS food must be discarded after seven days. A food handler finds a container of potato salad in the cooler that was made eight days ago. What should they do?
answers: Throw it away.
Taste it to see if it is still good.
Ask their manager what to do.
Put a new date on it and use it anyway.
feedbacks: Correct: The potato salad is past its use-by date and should be discarded.
Incorrect: You cannot taste, smell, or see bacteria.
Incorrect: The food handler should know the restaurant's policy and follow it.
Incorrect: This is a violation of the food safety policy.
questions.explanation: A food handler should always follow the restaurant's food safety policies. In this case, the potato salad is past its use-by date and must be discarded.

questions.question: A restaurant has a problem with fruit flies. Where are the fruit flies most likely to be coming from?
answers: The garbage cans.
The drains.
The lights.
The windows.
feedbacks: Correct: Fruit flies are attracted to the smell of rotting fruit and vegetables in the garbage.
Incorrect: Drain flies are a different type of fly.
Incorrect: Fruit flies are not attracted to light.
Incorrect: Fruit flies are small enough to get through screens, but they are not coming from the windows.
questions.explanation: Fruit flies are attracted to the smell of fermentation, which is why they are often found around garbage cans, drains, and overripe fruit.

questions.question: A food handler is preparing to start their shift. They are not feeling well and have a sore throat. What should they do?
answers: Go to work and see how they feel.
Call their manager and report their symptoms.
Take some medicine and go to work.
Ask a coworker to cover their shift.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This could put the health of the customers at risk.

Incorrect: The food handler should not self-medicate and go to work.
Incorrect: The food handler should still report their symptoms to the manager.
questions.explanation: A food handler who is not feeling well should always report their symptoms to their manager. The manager can then decide if the food handler is well enough to work and, if so, what tasks they can safely perform.

questions.question: A restaurant is receiving a delivery of frozen fish. The fish is covered in large ice crystals. What does this indicate?
answers: The fish is very fresh.
The fish has been thawed and refrozen.
The fish was frozen very quickly.
The fish is of high quality.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Large ice crystals are a sign of spoilage.
Correct: This is a sign of time-temperature abuse.
Incorrect: This would result in small ice crystals.
Incorrect: This is a sign of poor quality.
questions.explanation: Large ice crystals on a frozen food product are a sign that the product has been thawed and refrozen. This is a form of time-temperature abuse and can make the food unsafe to eat.

questions.question: A restaurant has a new employee who is a teenager. The manager is training the employee on food safety. What is the most important thing the manager should emphasize to the employee?
answers: The importance of washing their hands.
The importance of being on time for work.
The importance of smiling at the customers.
The importance of working hard.
feedbacks: Correct: Handwashing is the most important thing a food handler can do to prevent the spread of foodborne illness.
Incorrect: While important for the business, this is not a food safety issue.
Incorrect: This is a customer service issue, not a food safety issue.
Incorrect: While a good work ethic is important, it is not as important as food safety.
questions.explanation: Handwashing is the single most important thing a food handler can do to prevent the spread of foodborne illness. It is especially important to emphasize this to new employees who may not have had previous food safety training.

questions.question: Which of the following is a safe way to handle glassware?
answers: Stack the glasses to save space.
Carry the glasses by the rim.
Hold the glasses by the base.
Use a cloth towel to polish the glasses.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Stacking glasses can cause them to break.
Incorrect: This can contaminate the glasses.
Correct: This prevents your fingers from touching the rim of the glass.
Incorrect: A cloth towel can leave lint on the glasses and can also spread germs.
questions.explanation: To prevent contamination, glassware should be handled by the base, not by the rim.

questions.question: A restaurant is using a chemical sanitizer to sanitize a food-contact surface. The sanitizer must have a concentration of 50-99 ppm. What type of sanitizer is the restaurant most likely using?
answers: Chlorine
Iodine
Quaternary ammonium compound (quat)
Acid

Incorrect: The correct concentration for an iodine-based sanitizer is 12.5-25 ppm.
Incorrect: The correct concentration for a quat sanitizer is 200-400 ppm.
Incorrect: Acid sanitizers are not commonly used in food service establishments.
questions.explanation: A chlorine-based sanitizer is a common and effective sanitizer that is used in many food service establishments. The correct concentration for a chlorine sanitizer is 50-99 ppm.

questions.question: A restaurant has a policy that all employees must be trained in food safety. A new employee has just been hired. When should the employee be trained?
answers: Before they start working.
Within the first week of work.
Within the first month of work.
Whenever the manager has time.

Incorrect: The employee should be trained before they start working.

questions.explanation: All new employees should be trained in food safety before they start working. This will help to ensure that they do not contaminate food or cause a foodborne illness outbreak.

feedbacks: Incorrect: The freezing point of water is 32°F.

questions.question: A restaurant has a policy that all TCS food must be labeled with a use-by date. A food handler is preparing a batch of chili. The chili is made on Monday. What should the use-by date on the label be?
answers: Tuesday
Wednesday
Sunday
The following Monday
feedbacks: Incorrect: The shelf life of TCS food is seven days.
Incorrect: The shelf life of TCS food is seven days.
Correct: The day of preparation is day 1, so the use-by date would be the following Sunday.
Incorrect: The shelf life of TCS food is seven days.
questions.explanation: Ready-to-eat TCS food can be stored for a maximum of seven days at 41°F or lower. The count begins on the day the food was prepared.

questions.question: A restaurant has a problem with ants. The manager has called a pest control operator (PCO). What should the manager do before the PCO arrives?
answers: Clean up any spills or crumbs.
Move all of the food out of the kitchen.
Close the restaurant for the day.
Buy a can of ant spray and spray it around the kitchen.
feedbacks: Correct: This will make it easier for the PCO to find the source of the ant problem.
Incorrect: This is not necessary.
Incorrect: This is not necessary.
Incorrect: The PCO will have their own products and methods.
questions.explanation: Before a PCO arrives, the manager should do a thorough cleaning of the kitchen. This will remove any food sources for the ants and will make it easier for the PCO to do their job.

questions.question: A food handler is preparing to start their shift. They have a cold and are sneezing. What should they do?
answers: Go to work and wear a mask.
Call their manager and report their symptoms.
Take some cold medicine and go to work.
Ask a coworker to cover their shift.
feedbacks: Incorrect: A mask will not prevent the spread of germs from sneezing.

Incorrect: The food handler should not self-medicate and go to work.
