Incorrect: You do not know how long the eggs have been at an unsafe temperature.
Correct: Fresh shell eggs must be received at an air temperature of 45°F or lower.
Incorrect: The safety of the food is the primary concern, not the cost.
questions.explanation: Fresh shell eggs must be received at an air temperature of 45°F or lower. A temperature of 50°F is in the temperature danger zone, and the shipment should be rejected.

questions.question: A restaurant has a new manager who wants to make sure that the restaurant is in compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). What is the best way for the manager to do this?
answers: Review the ADA guidelines.
Conduct a self-inspection of the restaurant to identify any potential barriers to access.
Train the employees on the ADA.
Wait for a customer to complain about a barrier to access.
Assume that the restaurant is already in compliance.
Hope for the best.
feedbacks: Correct: The manager needs to know the specific requirements of the ADA.
Correct: This is a proactive way to identify and correct any problems.
Correct: The employees need to know what is expected of them.
Incorrect: The manager should be proactive and not wait for a complaint.
Incorrect: The new manager should not make any assumptions.
Incorrect: This is not a good strategy for compliance.
questions.explanation: A new manager should take a proactive approach to ADA compliance. This includes reviewing the ADA guidelines, conducting regular self-inspections, and training the employees.

questions.question: Which of the following is the best way to handle a situation where a customer has a guide dog?
answers: Tell the customer that they cannot bring the dog into the restaurant.
Ask the customer what the dog's disability is.
Allow the customer to bring the dog into the restaurant, as long as it is well-behaved.
Ask the customer to show you the dog's certification papers.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Guide dogs are allowed in restaurants.
Incorrect: You are not allowed to ask about a person's disability.
Correct: A guide dog must be under the control of its handler at all times.
Incorrect: You are not allowed to ask for certification papers.
questions.explanation: A guide dog is a type of service animal that has been trained to help a person who is blind or visually impaired. Guide dogs are allowed in restaurants and other public places. The dog must be under the control of its handler at all times.

questions.question: Which of the following is the best way to clean and sanitize a blender?
answers: Unplug the blender.
Disassemble the blender.
Wash the parts in a three-compartment sink.
Wipe the blender with a sanitizer wipe.
Spray the blender with a hose.
Leave the blender assembled and run it through the dishwasher.
feedbacks: Correct: This is the first step to ensure safety.
Correct: The blender must be disassembled to be cleaned and sanitized properly.
Correct: This is the proper way to wash and sanitize the parts of the blender.
Incorrect: Wiping is not enough to clean and sanitize the blender.
Incorrect: This can damage the blender and can also spread bacteria.
Incorrect: Not all parts of a blender may be dishwasher safe.
questions.explanation: The best way to clean and sanitize a blender is to unplug it, disassemble it, and wash the parts in a three-compartment sink.

questions.question: A food handler is preparing to start their shift. They have a small, uninfected cut on their finger. They have washed their hands and put on a bandage. What else should they do?
answers: Put on a single-use glove.
Put on a second bandage.
Start working.
Show the cut to their manager.
feedbacks: Correct: A glove will provide an extra layer of protection.
Incorrect: A second bandage is not necessary.
Incorrect: The food handler should put on a glove first.
Incorrect: The food handler should know how to handle a small cut.
questions.explanation: A food handler with a small, uninfected cut on their hand must wash their hands, cover the cut with a clean bandage, and then put on a single-use glove before starting work.

questions.question: A restaurant is receiving a delivery of fresh shell eggs. The eggs are grade A. What does this mean?
answers: The eggs are safe to eat.
The eggs are of high quality.
The eggs are from a local farm.
The eggs are organic.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The grade of an egg is an indicator of quality, not safety.
Correct: Grade A eggs have a firm yolk and a thick white.
Incorrect: The grade of an egg does not indicate its origin.
Incorrect: The grade of an egg does not indicate whether it is organic.
questions.explanation: The grade of an egg is an indicator of its quality. Grade A eggs are the highest quality, followed by grade B and grade C.

questions.question: A restaurant has a new manager who wants to create a food safety manual for the restaurant. What is the best way for the manager to do this?
answers: Use a template from a reputable source, such as the local health department or a food safety consulting company.
Customize the template to fit the specific needs of the restaurant.
Have the manual reviewed by a food safety expert.
Write the manual from scratch.
Copy the manual from another restaurant.
Don't worry about creating a manual.
feedbacks: Correct: A template can be a good starting point.
Correct: The manual should be tailored to the restaurant's specific operations.
Correct: A food safety expert can help to ensure that the manual is accurate and complete.
Incorrect: This is a lot of work and may not be necessary.
Incorrect: The manual may not be appropriate for your restaurant.
Incorrect: A food safety manual can be a valuable tool for training and for ensuring compliance.
questions.explanation: The best way to create a food safety manual is to use a template from a reputable source, customize it to fit the specific needs of the restaurant, and have it reviewed by a food safety expert.

questions.question: Which of the following is the best way to handle a customer who has a wheelchair?
answers: Tell the customer that they cannot come into the restaurant.
Ask the customer if they need any help.
Grab the wheelchair and start pushing it without asking.
Stare at the customer.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is a violation of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA).
Correct: This is a polite and helpful thing to do.
Incorrect: You should always ask before you touch someone's wheelchair.
Incorrect: This is rude and unprofessional.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a customer who has a wheelchair is to ask them if they need any help. If they do, you can offer to help them in any way you can.

questions.question: A restaurant has a problem with geese gathering near the entrance. What is the best way to get rid of the geese?
answers: Set some traps for the geese.
Call a pest control operator (PCO) who specializes in wildlife removal.
Use a scarecrow to frighten the geese away.
Feed the geese to lure them away from the entrance.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Trapping geese is not an effective way to get rid of them.
Correct: A PCO can help to remove the geese and to prevent them from coming back.
Correct: A scarecrow can be an effective deterrent.
Incorrect: This will only attract more geese.
questions.explanation: The best way to get rid of geese is to use a combination of methods, including calling a PCO and using a scarecrow.

questions.question: A food handler is preparing to start their shift. They have a small, uninfected cut on their finger. They have washed their hands, put on a bandage, and put on a glove. The glove gets a tear in it. What should they do?
answers: Take off the glove and put on a new one.
Take off the glove and continue to work without it.
Put a second glove on over the torn one.
Ignore the tear and continue to work.
feedbacks: Correct: A torn glove must be replaced.
Incorrect: The cut must be covered by a glove.
Incorrect: This is not a safe practice.
Incorrect: A torn glove can contaminate food.
questions.explanation: If a glove gets a tear in it, it must be removed and replaced with a new one. The food handler should also wash their hands before putting on the new glove.

questions.question: A restaurant is receiving a delivery of fresh produce. The produce is from a supplier that the manager has used for many years. The produce looks and smells fresh, but the delivery truck is not refrigerated. What should the manager do?
answers: Accept the delivery because the produce looks and smells fresh.
Reject the shipment.
Accept the delivery but at a discounted price.
Complain to the driver about the unrefrigerated truck.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The produce could be contaminated from the unrefrigerated truck.
Correct: All TCS food must be delivered in a refrigerated truck. While not all produce is TCS, it is a sign of a poor supplier practice.
Incorrect: The safety of the food is the primary concern, not the cost.
Correct: The manager should complain to the driver and also reject the shipment.
questions.explanation: All TCS food must be delivered in a refrigerated truck. Even for non-TCS produce, an unrefrigerated truck is a sign of a poor supplier practice, and the shipment should be rejected. The manager should also complain to the driver and the supplier.

questions.question: A restaurant has a new manager who wants to make sure that the restaurant's HACCP plan is up-to-date. What is the best way for the manager to do this?
answers: Review the HACCP plan on a regular basis.
Update the HACCP plan whenever there are any changes in the menu or the operation.
Have the HACCP plan reviewed by a third-party expert.
Assume that the HACCP plan is fine as it is.
Don't worry about the HACCP plan.
Throw away the old HACCP plan and start over.
feedbacks: Correct: The HACCP plan should be reviewed at least once a year.
Correct: The HACCP plan must be updated to reflect any changes.
Correct: A third-party expert can provide an objective assessment of the HACCP plan.
Incorrect: The HACCP plan must be reviewed and updated on a regular basis.
Incorrect: A HACCP plan is a legal requirement for some food service establishments.
Incorrect: This is not necessary.
questions.explanation: The best way to make sure that a restaurant's HACCP plan is up-to-date is to review it on a regular basis, update it whenever there are any changes, and have it reviewed by a third-party expert.

questions.question: A new restaurant is setting up its food safety program. Which of the following is the BEST example of a proactive approach to food safety management?
answers: Reacting to customer complaints about foodborne illness.
Creating a detailed HACCP plan.
Training employees only after a food safety incident.
Relying solely on local health department inspections.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is a reactive approach, not proactive.
Correct: A HACCP plan is a systematic, preventive approach to food safety.
Incorrect: Training should be ongoing and preventive.
Incorrect: While important, inspections are periodic checks, not a continuous management system.
questions.explanation: A Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point (HACCP) plan is a cornerstone of a proactive food safety management system. It identifies potential hazards and implements controls to prevent foodborne illness before it occurs.

questions.question: A chef is preparing a large batch of chicken salad for a catering event. The chicken was cooked and cooled yesterday. Today, the chef is chopping the chicken and mixing it with other ingredients. At what point is the chicken salad at the GREATEST risk for time-temperature abuse?
answers: While the cooked chicken is stored in the cooler overnight.
While the chicken is being chopped and mixed at room temperature.
Once the finished chicken salad is placed in the refrigerator.
During transport to the catering event in a refrigerated truck.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Proper cooling and storage minimize risk at this stage.
Correct: This is when the food is in the temperature danger zone for an extended period.
Incorrect: Refrigeration slows bacterial growth.
Incorrect: A refrigerated truck maintains a safe temperature.
questions.explanation: Time-temperature abuse occurs when food is held in the temperature danger zone (41°F to 135°F) for too long. Chopping and mixing at room temperature expose the food to this risk.

questions.question: A food handler has been diagnosed with a foodborne illness caused by Norovirus. What is the manager's MOST important responsibility?
answers: Allow the food handler to continue working as long as they wear gloves.
Tell the food handler to take over-the-counter medication and return to work.
Exclude the food handler from the operation.
Assign the food handler to non-food handling duties.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Gloves are not a substitute for proper handwashing and exclusion.
Incorrect: This does not address the risk of transmission.
Correct: Employees with a diagnosed illness from Norovirus must be excluded.
Incorrect: The risk of transmission is still too high.
questions.explanation: The FDA Food Code requires that food handlers diagnosed with Norovirus be excluded from the food establishment to prevent transmission to food and customers.

questions.question: A restaurant receives a shipment of fresh fish. The fish has a strong, fishy odor and the eyes are cloudy. What should the receiving employee do?
answers: Accept the fish but cook it immediately.
Accept the fish and store it in the freezer.
Reject the shipment.
Accept the fish but at a discounted price.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Cooking may not eliminate all hazards from spoiled fish.
Incorrect: Freezing does not improve the quality of spoiled fish.
Correct: These are signs of spoilage and the fish should be rejected.
Incorrect: The safety of the food is the primary concern, not the cost.
questions.explanation: Fresh fish should have a mild ocean or seaweed scent and clear, bright eyes. A strong fishy odor and cloudy eyes are indicators of spoilage and the shipment should be rejected.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a physical contaminant in food?
answers: Sanitizer from a spray bottle.
A piece of a metal can.
Toxin from a poisonous mushroom.
Bacteria from unwashed hands.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is a chemical contaminant.
Correct: Physical contaminants are foreign objects that can cause injury.
Incorrect: This is a biological contaminant (toxin).
Incorrect: This is a biological contaminant.
questions.explanation: Physical contaminants are foreign objects that can get into food, such as metal, glass, or plastic. A piece of a metal can is a classic example.

questions.question: A restaurant is installing a new walk-in cooler. To ensure proper air circulation and temperature control, where should the shelving be located?
answers: Directly on the floor.
At least 6 inches off the floor and away from the walls.
As close to the ceiling as possible to maximize space.
Touching the walls to provide extra support.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This prevents proper cleaning and air circulation.
Correct: This allows for adequate air circulation and cleaning.
Incorrect: This can impede airflow from the evaporator coils.
Incorrect: This blocks air circulation and can create areas where the temperature is not maintained.
questions.explanation: Shelving in a walk-in cooler should be at least 6 inches off the floor and away from the walls to allow for proper air circulation, which is essential for maintaining a consistent and safe temperature, and to facilitate cleaning.

questions.question: A food handler is tasked with cleaning and sanitizing a cutting board that has been used for raw chicken. What are the correct steps in the proper order?
answers: Rinse, sanitize, wash, air-dry.
Wash, rinse, sanitize, air-dry.
Sanitize, wash, rinse, air-dry.
Wash, sanitize, rinse, air-dry.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Washing must come before sanitizing.
Correct: This is the correct four-step process for cleaning and sanitizing.
Incorrect: Sanitizing before washing is ineffective.
Incorrect: Rinsing after sanitizing can re-contaminate the surface.
questions.explanation: The proper procedure for cleaning and sanitizing food-contact surfaces is to first wash with soap and water, then rinse with clean water, then apply a sanitizer for the correct amount of time, and finally allow the surface to air-dry.

questions.question: A manager notices that a food handler has a sore throat and a fever. The operation primarily serves a high-risk population. What should the manager do?
answers: Allow the food handler to work but only with non-food contact surfaces.
Send the food handler home and require a doctor's note to return.
Tell the food handler to wear a mask and continue working.
Have the food handler take their temperature every hour.
feedbacks: Incorrect: With a high-risk population, the risk of transmission is too great.
Correct: When serving a high-risk population, a food handler with a sore throat and fever must be excluded.
Incorrect: A mask is not sufficient to prevent transmission in this situation.
Incorrect: This is not a substitute for exclusion.
questions.explanation: For operations that primarily serve a high-risk population, a food handler with a sore throat and fever must be excluded from the operation to prevent the spread of illness. A doctor's note is required for them to return to work.

questions.question: A restaurant is experiencing a pest infestation. Which of the following is the MOST important step in an Integrated Pest Management (IPM) program?
answers: Setting out traps to catch pests.
Spraying pesticides regularly.
Denying pests access, food, and shelter.
Hiring a pest control operator (PCO) immediately.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Traps are a control measure, but not the most important first step.
Incorrect: Pesticides should be used as a last resort and applied by a licensed professional.
Correct: This is the foundation of an effective IPM program.
Incorrect: While a PCO is a key part of an IPM program, prevention is the most important step.
questions.explanation: The most critical component of an Integrated Pest Management (IPM) program is to deny pests access to the establishment and to deny them food and shelter. This proactive approach is more effective than simply trying to eliminate pests once they are present.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) food?

Cooked rice

Sprouts

Correct: Whole, raw vegetables are generally not TCS foods.
Incorrect: Sprouts are a TCS food due to the high risk of bacterial contamination.
questions.explanation: Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) foods are those that support the rapid growth of bacteria. While many fruits and vegetables become TCS once cut, whole, raw carrots are not considered a TCS food.

questions.question: A restaurant wants to start making its own fresh-squeezed orange juice. What is a key food safety concern the manager needs to address?
answers: The acidity of the juice will prevent all bacterial growth.
The juice must be pasteurized or have a warning label.
The color of the oranges indicates their safety.
The juice can be stored at room temperature for up to 24 hours.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While acidity can slow growth, it does not prevent it entirely, especially for certain pathogens.
Correct: Unpasteurized juice is a high-risk item and requires either pasteurization or a consumer advisory.
Incorrect: The color of the oranges is not a reliable indicator of microbial safety.
Incorrect: Fresh juice is a TCS food and must be refrigerated.
questions.explanation: According to the FDA Food Code, fresh juice prepared in a food establishment must either be pasteurized to eliminate pathogens or be served with a warning label informing consumers of the risks of consuming unpasteurized products.

questions.question: A chef is cooling a large stockpot of soup. Which method will cool the soup the fastest and most safely?
answers: Placing the hot stockpot directly into the walk-in cooler.
Leaving the soup on the counter to cool to room temperature before refrigerating.
Dividing the soup into smaller, shallow pans and placing them in an ice-water bath.
Adding a large block of ice to the soup.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This can raise the ambient temperature of the cooler and put other foods at risk.
Incorrect: This allows the soup to remain in the temperature danger zone for too long.
Correct: This increases the surface area and uses a rapid cooling method.
Incorrect: While this can help, it will also dilute the soup and may not cool it evenly or quickly enough.
questions.explanation: The most effective way to cool a large quantity of a hot liquid is to increase the surface area by dividing it into smaller containers and to use a rapid cooling method like an ice-water bath.

questions.question: A food handler is wearing single-use gloves to assemble sandwiches. They are interrupted by a coworker and go to take out the trash. What should the food handler do before returning to their task?
answers: Wash their hands with the gloves on.
Keep the same gloves on to save time.
Remove the gloves, wash their hands, and put on a new pair of gloves.
Remove the gloves and put on a new pair without washing their hands.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Gloves should be changed, and hands should be washed.

Correct: This is the proper procedure to prevent cross-contamination.
Incorrect: Hands must be washed after a task that could cause contamination and before putting on new gloves.
questions.explanation: Single-use gloves are for a single task. After taking out the trash, the food handler's gloves are contaminated. They must be removed, hands must be washed, and a new pair of gloves must be put on before resuming food preparation.

questions.question: A shipment of vacuum-sealed smoked salmon arrives at a temperature of 45°F. What should the receiving employee do?
answers: Accept the shipment because it is a smoked product.
Accept the shipment and immediately place it in the freezer.
Reject the shipment.
Accept the shipment but use it within 24 hours.

Incorrect: The product has already been in the temperature danger zone.
Correct: Cold TCS food must be received at 41°F or lower.
Incorrect: The time in the temperature danger zone is unknown, making it unsafe.
questions.explanation: Cold TCS food, including smoked salmon, must be received at a temperature of 41°F or lower. A temperature of 45°F is in the temperature danger zone, and the shipment should be rejected.

questions.question: Which of the following is a common food allergen?
answers: Chicken
Soy
Broccoli
Pork
feedbacks: Incorrect: While some people may have sensitivities, chicken is not one of the major food allergens.
Correct: Soy is one of the eight major food allergens identified by the FDA.

questions.explanation: The FDA has identified eight major food allergens: milk, eggs, fish, crustacean shellfish, tree nuts, peanuts, wheat, and soybeans.

questions.question: A restaurant is designing a new kitchen. Which of the following flooring materials is the BEST choice for the food preparation area?
answers: Unglazed ceramic tile
Sealed concrete
Hardwood
High-pile carpeting
feedbacks: Incorrect: The porous nature of unglazed tile can harbor bacteria.
Correct: Sealed concrete is non-porous, durable, and easy to clean.
Incorrect: Wood is absorbent and difficult to sanitize.
Incorrect: Carpeting is not allowed in food preparation areas because it is impossible to properly clean and sanitize.
questions.explanation: Flooring in food preparation areas must be smooth, non-absorbent, durable, and easy to clean. Sealed concrete meets all of these criteria.

questions.question: What is the correct concentration for an iodine-based sanitizer?
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is the concentration for a chlorine-based sanitizer.
Correct: This is the recommended concentration for an iodine-based sanitizer.
Incorrect: This is the concentration for a quaternary ammonium compound (quat) sanitizer.

questions.explanation: The proper concentration for an iodine-based sanitizer is 12.5-25 parts per million (ppm). It is crucial to use test strips to verify the concentration of any sanitizer.

questions.question: A food handler has a cut on their finger. What is the correct procedure for them to follow to safely handle food?
answers: Wash the cut with soap and water and continue working.
Cover the cut with a bandage.
Cover the cut with a bandage and a single-use glove.
Apply an antiseptic and continue working.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The cut must be covered to prevent contamination.
Incorrect: A bandage alone is not sufficient.
Correct: The cut must be covered with a clean bandage and then a single-use glove.
Incorrect: The cut must be properly covered.
questions.explanation: A cut on a food handler's hand must be covered with a clean bandage and then a single-use glove to prevent any potential contamination of the food.

questions.question: Which of the following is a sign of a cockroach infestation?
answers: Gnaw marks on food packaging.
A strong, oily odor.
Scraps of paper and cloth in a corner.
Tracks on a dusty surface.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is a sign of a rodent infestation.
Correct: Cockroaches produce a strong, oily odor.
Incorrect: This is a sign of a rodent nesting.
Incorrect: This is more indicative of rodents.
questions.explanation: Signs of a cockroach infestation include a strong, oily odor, droppings that look like grains of black pepper, and capsule-shaped egg cases.

questions.question: Which food is safe to eat if cooked to a minimum internal temperature of 145°F for 15 seconds?

A ground beef patty
A pork chop
A stuffed pasta shell
feedbacks: Incorrect: Poultry must be cooked to 165°F.
Incorrect: Ground meat must be cooked to 155°F.
Correct: Whole cuts of meat like pork chops need to be cooked to 145°F for 15 seconds.
Incorrect: Stuffed items must be cooked to 165°F.
questions.explanation: The FDA Food Code requires that whole cuts of pork, beef, veal, and lamb be cooked to a minimum internal temperature of 145°F for 15 seconds.

questions.question: A restaurant manager is creating a crisis management plan. Which of the following should be included?
answers: A list of employees' social media accounts.
A plan for communicating with the media.
A schedule for daily cleaning tasks.
The menu for the upcoming week.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is not a necessary component of a crisis management plan.
Correct: Effective communication is crucial during a crisis.
Incorrect: While important for food safety, this is part of standard operating procedures, not a crisis plan.
Incorrect: This is not relevant to crisis management.
questions.explanation: A comprehensive crisis management plan should include procedures for dealing with the crisis itself, as well as a plan for communicating with staff, customers, and the media.

questions.question: A chef is making a hollandaise sauce. The recipe uses raw egg yolks. What is the safest way to prepare this sauce?
answers: Use regular shell eggs and cook the sauce to 135°F.
Use pasteurized eggs.
Use organic, free-range eggs.
Add a small amount of vinegar to the sauce to kill bacteria.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This temperature is not high enough to ensure the destruction of Salmonella.
Correct: Pasteurized eggs have been heat-treated to destroy pathogens.
Incorrect: The source of the eggs does not guarantee they are free from Salmonella.
Incorrect: Vinegar is not a reliable method for eliminating Salmonella in this context.
questions.explanation: When preparing dishes with raw or undercooked eggs, it is safest to use pasteurized eggs, which have been treated to eliminate potential pathogens like Salmonella.

questions.question: A food handler is reheating a container of leftover chili for the hot-holding unit. What is the minimum internal temperature the chili must reach, and for how long?
answers: 145°F for 15 seconds
155°F for 15 seconds
165°F for 15 seconds
135°F for 15 seconds
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is the cooking temperature for whole cuts of meat.
Incorrect: This is the cooking temperature for ground meat.
Correct: All reheated TCS food must reach an internal temperature of 165°F for 15 seconds.
Incorrect: This is the minimum hot-holding temperature, not the reheating temperature.
questions.explanation: TCS food that is being reheated for hot-holding must reach a minimum internal temperature of 165°F for 15 seconds within two hours.

questions.question: A restaurant has a self-service buffet. Which of the following is a critical food safety practice for the buffet?
answers: Allowing customers to reuse their plates.
Providing a separate utensil for each food item.
Keeping all food at room temperature to encourage grazing.
Mixing fresh food with food that has been on the buffet for a while.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This can lead to cross-contamination.
Correct: This prevents cross-contamination between different food items.
Incorrect: TCS food must be held at the proper hot or cold temperatures.
Incorrect: This is not a safe practice and can lead to time-temperature abuse.
questions.explanation: To prevent cross-contamination at a self-service buffet, a separate, clean utensil should be provided for each food item.

questions.question: A delivery of live oysters arrives with a shellstock identification tag. How long must the tag be kept on file after the last oyster from the container is sold or served?

60 days
90 days
120 days
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is not the correct time frame.
Incorrect: This is not the correct time frame.
Correct: The shellstock identification tag must be kept for 90 days.
Incorrect: This is not the correct time frame.
questions.explanation: The shellstock identification tag for live shellfish must be kept on file for 90 days from the date the last shellfish from the container was sold or served. This is to aid in tracing the source of the shellfish in case of a foodborne illness outbreak.

questions.question: Which of the following is the BEST way to prevent the spread of viruses in a food service operation?
answers: Cooking food to the proper internal temperature.
Practicing good personal hygiene, especially handwashing.
Freezing food for at least 30 days.
Using a sanitizer on all food-contact surfaces.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While important for killing bacteria, cooking may not inactivate all viruses.
Correct: Viruses are most commonly spread through poor personal hygiene.
Incorrect: Freezing does not reliably kill viruses.
Incorrect: While helpful, this is not the primary way to prevent the spread of viruses from person to person.
questions.explanation: The most effective way to prevent the spread of foodborne viruses, such as Norovirus and Hepatitis A, is through rigorous personal hygiene practices, most importantly, frequent and proper handwashing.

questions.question: A restaurant is using a three-compartment sink for manual dishwashing. What should the third compartment be used for?
answers: Washing
Rinsing
Sanitizing
Air-drying
feedbacks: Incorrect: Washing is done in the first compartment.
Incorrect: Rinsing is done in the second compartment.
Correct: The third compartment is for sanitizing the dishes.
Incorrect: Dishes should be air-dried on a clean and sanitized drainboard.
questions.explanation: In a three-compartment sink, the first compartment is for washing, the second is for rinsing, and the third is for sanitizing.

questions.question: A food handler has been vomiting. They should be excluded from the operation until they have been symptom-free for at least how long?
answers: 12 hours
24 hours
36 hours
48 hours
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is not a long enough period.
Correct: The FDA Food Code requires an employee to be symptom-free for at least 24 hours before returning to work.
Incorrect: This is longer than the required period.
Incorrect: While some jurisdictions may require a longer period, the standard is 24 hours.
questions.explanation: A food handler who has been vomiting or has had diarrhea must be excluded from the operation and cannot return to work until they have been symptom-free for at least 24 hours.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a backflow prevention device?
answers: To increase the water pressure in the pipes.
To prevent the reverse flow of contaminated water into the potable water supply.
To filter impurities from the incoming water.
To measure the amount of water being used.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is not the function of a backflow prevention device.
Correct: This is the critical function of a backflow prevention device.
Incorrect: While water filters do this, it is not the purpose of a backflow prevention device.
Incorrect: This is the function of a water meter.
questions.explanation: A backflow prevention device, such as an air gap or a vacuum breaker, is essential for preventing contaminated water from a non-potable source from flowing backward into the clean, potable water supply.

questions.question: Which of the following foods must be cooked to a minimum internal temperature of 155°F for 15 seconds?
answers: A salmon steak
A chicken breast
A ground beef burger
A roast beef
feedbacks: Incorrect: Fish should be cooked to 145°F.
Incorrect: Poultry must be cooked to 165°F.
Correct: Ground meat must be cooked to 155°F for 15 seconds.
Incorrect: The cooking temperature for roasts depends on the type of roast and the oven temperature.
questions.explanation: The FDA Food Code requires that ground meat, including beef, pork, and other meats, be cooked to a minimum internal temperature of 155°F for 15 seconds to destroy harmful bacteria.

questions.question: A restaurant discovers that a recent shipment of lettuce has been recalled due to a potential E. coli contamination. What should the manager do FIRST?
answers: Cook the lettuce thoroughly to kill the E. coli.
Immediately discard all of the recalled lettuce.
Mix the recalled lettuce with a new batch of lettuce to dilute any potential contamination.
Continue to serve the lettuce but inform customers of the recall.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The lettuce should not be used at all.
Correct: The first step is to remove the recalled product from the food supply.
Incorrect: This would contaminate the new lettuce.
Incorrect: This would knowingly put customers at risk.
questions.explanation: Upon learning of a food recall, the manager's first and most important action is to identify and remove the recalled product from inventory to prevent it from being served to customers.

questions.question: Which of the following is a safe way to thaw a frozen turkey?
answers: On the kitchen counter overnight.
In a microwave, if it will be cooked immediately after.
In a sink of hot water.
In a warm oven.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This allows the outer layers of the turkey to be in the temperature danger zone for too long.
Correct: Thawing in a microwave is safe as long as the turkey is cooked immediately afterward.
Incorrect: Hot water can raise the surface temperature of the turkey into the temperature danger zone.
Incorrect: This is not a safe thawing method.
questions.explanation: There are three safe methods for thawing frozen food: in the refrigerator, under cold running water, or in a microwave if the food will be cooked immediately after thawing.

questions.question: A food handler is making a tuna salad and has a cut on their hand. They are wearing a bandage and a single-use glove. When should they change their glove and wash their hands?
answers: Only if the glove tears.
Every four hours of continuous use.
At the end of their shift.
After they finish making the tuna salad.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Gloves should be changed more frequently.
Correct: Gloves should be changed at least every four hours, or more often if necessary.
Incorrect: This is too long and increases the risk of contamination.
Incorrect: If the task is long, the gloves should be changed during the process.
questions.explanation: Single-use gloves should be changed at least every four hours of continuous use, or more frequently if they become soiled or torn, or when changing tasks.

questions.question: What is the maximum temperature at which cold TCS food should be stored?
feedbacks: Incorrect: While safe, this is colder than necessary and may not be practical for all cold foods.
Correct: Cold TCS food must be stored at 41°F or lower.
Incorrect: This is in the temperature danger zone.
Incorrect: This is well into the temperature danger zone.
questions.explanation: To prevent the growth of harmful bacteria, cold TCS food must be stored at an internal temperature of 41°F or lower.

questions.question: A customer has a severe allergic reaction after eating a meal at a restaurant. What should the manager do first?
answers: Call 911.
Offer the customer a free meal.
Ask the customer what they ate.
Fill out an incident report.
feedbacks: Correct: The immediate priority is the health and safety of the customer.
Incorrect: This does not address the immediate medical emergency.
Incorrect: While important for the investigation, this is not the first priority.
Incorrect: This should be done after the immediate medical needs of the customer have been addressed.
questions.explanation: If a customer has an allergic reaction, the first and most critical step is to call for emergency medical assistance.

questions.question: What is the best way to check the temperature of a food?
answers: Touch the food with your hand.
Use a clean and sanitized thermometer.
Observe the color of the food.
Time how long the food has been cooking.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is not an accurate or safe way to measure temperature.
Correct: A calibrated thermometer is the only reliable way to measure the internal temperature of food.
Incorrect: The color of the food is not a reliable indicator of its internal temperature.
Incorrect: Cooking time is a guideline, but the internal temperature must be verified.
questions.explanation: To ensure food has reached a safe internal temperature, it is essential to use a clean and sanitized thermometer and to insert it into the thickest part of the food.

questions.question: Which of the following is an acceptable material for a cutting board?
answers: Hardwood
Polyethylene
Glass
Ceramic
feedbacks: Incorrect: While some hardwoods are acceptable, they can be difficult to clean and sanitize.
Correct: Polyethylene (plastic) is a common and acceptable material for cutting boards because it is non-absorbent and easy to clean.
Incorrect: Glass cutting boards can dull knives and are not recommended.
Incorrect: Ceramic cutting boards can also dull knives.
questions.explanation: Cutting boards should be made of a non-absorbent material that is easy to clean and sanitize. Polyethylene is a widely used and approved material.

questions.question: A food handler is cleaning a meat slicer. What is the final step they should take before reassembling the slicer?
answers: Wash the parts in hot, soapy water.
Rinse the parts with clean water.
Sanitize the parts with an approved sanitizer.
Allow the parts to air-dry.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is the first step in the cleaning process.
Incorrect: This is the second step.
Incorrect: This is the third step.
Correct: After washing, rinsing, and sanitizing, the parts should be allowed to air-dry completely before reassembly.
questions.explanation: The proper order for cleaning and sanitizing food-contact surfaces, including a meat slicer, is to wash, rinse, sanitize, and then air-dry.

questions.question: A manager is training a new employee on the proper use of a three-compartment sink. What should the manager tell the employee about the water temperature in the first compartment?
answers: It should be as hot as you can stand.
It should be at least 110°F.
It should be at least 171°F.
The temperature does not matter as long as you use soap.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is not a precise or safe measurement.
Correct: The water in the wash compartment should be at least 110°F.
Incorrect: This is the temperature for hot water sanitizing, not washing.
Incorrect: The water temperature is important for effective cleaning.
questions.explanation: For manual dishwashing in a three-compartment sink, the water in the first compartment (for washing) must be at least 110°F.

questions.question: Which of the following is a requirement for a handwashing station?
answers: A common cloth towel for drying hands.
Hot and cold running water.
A bar of soap.
A waste container that must be touched to be opened.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Only single-use paper towels or a hand dryer are acceptable.
Correct: A handwashing station must have both hot and cold running water.
Incorrect: While soap is required, a bar of soap can become contaminated. Liquid soap is preferred.
Incorrect: The waste container should be hands-free if possible.
questions.explanation: An acceptable handwashing station must have hot and cold running water, soap (preferably liquid), a way to dry hands (single-use paper towels or a hand dryer), and a waste container.

questions.question: A restaurant is located in an area that is under a boil water advisory. What should the manager do?
answers: Continue to use the tap water for drinking and cooking.
Boil all water for at least one minute before using it.
Use bottled water for drinking but continue to use tap water for cooking.
Close the restaurant until the advisory is lifted.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This could lead to a foodborne illness outbreak.
Correct: During a boil water advisory, all water used for drinking, cooking, and washing must be boiled for at least one minute.
Incorrect: All water that comes into contact with food must be safe.
Incorrect: While closing is an option, there are ways to continue operating safely, such as boiling water or using bottled water.
questions.explanation: In the event of a boil water advisory, food establishments must take precautions to ensure the safety of their water supply. This includes boiling all water for at least one minute or using an approved alternative source of water, such as bottled water.

questions.question: A chef is preparing a dish that contains a common allergen. What is the best way to prevent cross-contact?
answers: Cook the dish at a high temperature to destroy the allergen.
Use the same utensils for all dishes but wipe them clean between uses.
Prepare the allergen-containing dish in a separate area with separate utensils.
Inform the customer that there is a risk of cross-contact.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Cooking does not destroy allergens.
Incorrect: Wiping is not sufficient to remove allergens.
Correct: The best way to prevent cross-contact is to use separate equipment and work areas.
Incorrect: While this is a good practice, the primary goal is to prevent cross-contact in the first place.
questions.explanation: To prevent cross-contact of allergens, it is essential to use separate cooking equipment, utensils, and preparation areas for allergen-containing foods.

questions.question: A food handler is taking the temperature of a roast. Where should they insert the thermometer to get an accurate reading?
answers: In the thickest part of the roast.
In the thinnest part of the roast.
On the surface of the roast.
In a bone.
feedbacks: Correct: This ensures that the entire roast has reached the minimum internal temperature.
Incorrect: This will not give an accurate reading of the overall temperature.
Incorrect: The surface temperature is not a reliable indicator of the internal temperature.
Incorrect: The thermometer should be inserted into the meat, not a bone.
questions.explanation: To get an accurate temperature reading of a food item, the thermometer should be inserted into the thickest part of the food, away from any bones.

questions.question: A restaurant is storing raw ground beef, raw fish, and raw chicken in a walk-in cooler. What is the correct top-to-bottom storage order?
answers: Chicken, fish, beef
Fish, beef, chicken
Beef, chicken, fish
The order does not matter as long as the foods are on separate shelves.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This order increases the risk of cross-contamination.
Correct: This order is based on the minimum internal cooking temperatures of the foods.
Incorrect: This order is incorrect.
Incorrect: The order is critical to prevent cross-contamination.
questions.explanation: To prevent cross-contamination in a cooler, food should be stored in the following top-to-bottom order based on their minimum internal cooking temperatures: ready-to-eat food, seafood, whole cuts of beef and pork, ground meat and fish, and whole and ground poultry. In this case, the correct order is fish, beef, and then chicken on the bottom.

questions.question: What is the purpose of an air gap?
answers: To create a space between the faucet and the flood rim of a sink to prevent backflow.
To allow air to circulate in a dry storage area.
To provide ventilation in a kitchen.
To create a barrier to prevent pests from entering the building.
feedbacks: Correct: An air gap is a physical separation that prevents contaminated water from entering the potable water supply.
Incorrect: While air circulation is important, this is not the purpose of an air gap in the context of plumbing.
Incorrect: This is the purpose of a ventilation system.
Incorrect: While important, this is not the function of an air gap.
questions.explanation: An air gap is the most reliable method for preventing backflow. It is the vertical distance between the outlet of a faucet and the flood-level rim of a sink.

questions.question: Which of the following is a sign that a shipment of canned goods should be rejected?
answers: The cans are at room temperature.
The cans have a dent on the seam.
The labels are slightly faded.
The cans are from a well-known brand.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Canned goods are shelf-stable and can be stored at room temperature.
Correct: A dent on a seam can damage the seal of the can and allow for the entry of bacteria.
Incorrect: While not ideal, a faded label does not necessarily indicate a safety issue.
Incorrect: The brand of a canned good is not a guarantee of its safety.
questions.explanation: Canned goods should be inspected upon delivery and rejected if they have any signs of damage, such as a dent on a seam, a swollen top or bottom, or rust.

questions.question: A food handler has been sick with diarrhea. They are symptom-free for 24 hours and want to return to work. What must they have before they can resume their normal duties?
answers: A note from their doctor.
A new uniform.
A signed statement that they are feeling better.
A negative stool sample.
feedbacks: Correct: In most jurisdictions, a doctor's note is required for an employee to return to work after being sick with a foodborne illness.
Incorrect: While a clean uniform is important, it is not a requirement for returning to work after an illness.
Incorrect: This is not sufficient documentation.
Incorrect: While this may be required in some outbreak situations, it is not a standard requirement for returning to work.
questions.explanation: An employee who has been excluded due to a foodborne illness must provide a written release from a medical professional before they can return to work.

questions.question: A restaurant is using a hot-holding unit to keep food warm. What is the minimum temperature at which the food should be held?
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is in the temperature danger zone.
Correct: Hot TCS food must be held at 135°F or higher.
Incorrect: While this temperature is safe, it is higher than the minimum requirement.
Incorrect: This is the reheating temperature, not the hot-holding temperature.
questions.explanation: To prevent the growth of bacteria, hot TCS food must be held at an internal temperature of 135°F or higher.

questions.question: A manager is conducting a food safety audit of their operation. Which of the following is an example of a critical control point (CCP) for a dish of grilled chicken breasts?
answers: The temperature of the walk-in cooler where the chicken is stored.
The internal temperature of the chicken after cooking.
The personal hygiene of the food handler preparing the chicken.
The cleanliness of the plate the chicken is served on.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While important for storage, the cooking step is the CCP for eliminating pathogens.
Correct: This is the point where the hazard of bacterial contamination can be eliminated.
Incorrect: While important, the cooking step is the specific CCP for this hazard.
Incorrect: While important, the cooking step is the CCP for the raw chicken.
questions.explanation: In a HACCP plan for grilled chicken, the critical control point is the final cooking step, where the chicken must reach a minimum internal temperature of 165°F to kill any harmful bacteria.

questions.question: A restaurant is closed for a week for renovations. When it reopens, what should the manager do with the TCS food that was in the cooler?
answers: Check the temperature of the food and if it is still at 41°F or below, it is safe to use.
Cook all of the food to a high temperature to make it safe.
Discard all of the TCS food.
Donate the food to a local shelter.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The food has been in the cooler for too long.
Incorrect: Cooking may not destroy all toxins that may have been produced by bacteria.
Correct: TCS food that has been stored for more than seven days should be discarded.
Incorrect: Food that is not safe for customers is not safe for donation.
questions.explanation: Ready-to-eat TCS food can be stored for a maximum of seven days at 41°F or lower. After this time, it must be discarded.

questions.question: Which of the following is a chemical contaminant?
answers: A fly in a bowl of soup.
Pesticide residue on a head of lettuce.
Mold on a piece of bread.
A piece of glass in a salad.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is a physical contaminant.
Correct: Pesticides are chemicals that can be harmful if consumed.
Incorrect: This is a biological contaminant.
Incorrect: This is a physical contaminant.
questions.explanation: Chemical contaminants are chemical substances that can contaminate food. Pesticides are a common example of a chemical contaminant.

questions.question: What is the best way to dry hands after washing them?
answers: On your apron.
With a common cloth towel.
With a single-use paper towel or a hand dryer.
By waving them in the air.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This can contaminate your hands.
Incorrect: A common towel can spread germs.
Correct: These are the only two approved methods for drying hands.
Incorrect: This is not an effective or sanitary way to dry hands.
questions.explanation: Hands should be dried with a single-use paper towel or a hand dryer to prevent re-contamination.

questions.question: A restaurant is preparing a large batch of potato salad. The potatoes have been cooked and cooled. The salad is being mixed at room temperature. How long can the potato salad be in the temperature danger zone before it must be discarded?
answers: 2 hours
4 hours
6 hours
8 hours
feedbacks: Incorrect: While it is best to minimize time in the danger zone, the maximum is longer.
Correct: The total time that a TCS food can be in the temperature danger zone is four hours.
Incorrect: This is too long and the food would be unsafe.
Incorrect: This is far too long and the food would be unsafe.
questions.explanation: TCS food can be in the temperature danger zone (41°F to 135°F) for a maximum of four hours before it must be discarded.

questions.question: A restaurant has a no-smoking policy, but a manager sees an employee smoking in the dry storage area. What should the manager do?
answers: Ignore it, as long as the employee is not smoking in the food preparation area.
Tell the employee to put out the cigarette and remind them of the no-smoking policy.
Ask the employee to smoke outside.
Join the employee for a cigarette.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Smoking is not allowed in any area of the food establishment.
Correct: The manager must enforce the no-smoking policy.
Incorrect: While this is the correct action, the manager should also address the policy violation.
Incorrect: This is a violation of food safety regulations and a poor example for the employee.
questions.explanation: Smoking is prohibited in all areas of a food establishment, including storage areas. The manager must address the policy violation with the employee.

questions.question: Which of the following is the most effective way to prevent cross-contamination between raw meat and ready-to-eat food?
answers: Washing your hands after handling raw meat.
Using a separate cutting board for raw meat and ready-to-eat food.
Rinsing the cutting board with hot water after using it for raw meat.
Cooking the ready-to-eat food to a high temperature.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While important, this is not the most effective way to prevent cross-contamination on surfaces.
Correct: Using separate equipment is the best way to prevent cross-contamination.
Incorrect: Rinsing is not enough to remove all bacteria. The cutting board must be washed and sanitized.
Incorrect: Ready-to-eat food is not typically cooked.
questions.explanation: The most effective way to prevent cross-contamination is to use separate equipment, including cutting boards and utensils, for raw and ready-to-eat foods.

questions.question: A restaurant is located in a building that has been flooded. What is the most important thing for the manager to do?
answers: Start cleaning up the water immediately.
Contact the local regulatory authority.
Throw away any food that got wet.
Try to salvage as much food as possible to minimize losses.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The first priority is to ensure the safety of the food.
Correct: The manager must report the flood to the local health department and get their approval before reopening.
Incorrect: While this is important, contacting the health department is the first step.
Incorrect: The safety of the food is the primary concern, not the financial loss.
questions.explanation: In the event of a flood, a food establishment must cease operations and notify the local regulatory authority. The establishment cannot reopen until it has been inspected and approved by the health department.

questions.question: A food handler is displaying symptoms of jaundice. What should the manager do?
answers: Allow the food handler to work as long as they wear gloves and a mask.
Send the food handler home and report the illness to the local regulatory authority.
Tell the food handler to see a doctor and return to work when they feel better.
Assign the food handler to cleaning duties.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Jaundice is a symptom of Hepatitis A, and the employee must be excluded.
Correct: Jaundice must be reported to the health department, and the employee must be excluded.
Incorrect: The manager has a responsibility to report the illness.
Incorrect: The employee must be excluded from the operation entirely.
questions.explanation: Jaundice (yellowing of the skin and eyes) is a symptom of Hepatitis A. An employee with jaundice must be excluded from the operation, and the illness must be reported to the local regulatory authority.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a pest control operator (PCO)?
answers: To sell pesticides to the restaurant.
To identify and eliminate pests from the establishment.
To train the restaurant staff on how to use pesticides.
To conduct the restaurant's daily pest inspections.
feedbacks: Incorrect: A PCO provides a service, not just products.
Correct: A PCO is a licensed professional who can help prevent and control pest infestations.
Incorrect: Only licensed PCOs should apply pesticides.
Incorrect: The restaurant staff should be conducting daily inspections as part of the IPM program.
questions.explanation: A pest control operator (PCO) is a licensed professional who can help a food establishment develop and implement an Integrated Pest Management (IPM) program to prevent and control pests.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a biological contaminant?
answers: A shard of glass.
A sanitizer solution.
Norovirus.
A metal shaving.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is a physical contaminant.
Incorrect: This is a chemical contaminant.
Correct: Norovirus is a virus that can cause foodborne illness.
Incorrect: This is a physical contaminant.
questions.explanation: Biological contaminants are living organisms, such as bacteria, viruses, fungi, and parasites, that can cause foodborne illness.

questions.question: A food handler is preparing salads. They are not wearing gloves. Is this a violation of food safety regulations?
answers: Yes, gloves must be worn at all times when handling food.
No, as long as the food handler has clean hands.
Yes, unless the establishment has an approved written policy for bare-hand contact with ready-to-eat food.
No, because salads are not a TCS food.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Gloves are not always required.
Incorrect: Bare-hand contact with ready-to-eat food is generally not allowed.
Correct: Bare-hand contact with ready-to-eat food is prohibited unless the establishment has a specific written policy in place that is approved by the regulatory authority.
Incorrect: Some salads can be TCS foods, and bare-hand contact with any ready-to-eat food is a concern.
questions.explanation: The FDA Food Code prohibits bare-hand contact with ready-to-eat food. However, an establishment may be granted an exception if it has a written policy that has been approved by the local regulatory authority and meets certain conditions.

questions.question: A restaurant is cooling a large pot of beef stew. It has been two hours, and the temperature of the stew has dropped from 135°F to 85°F. Is this acceptable?
answers: Yes, as long as the stew reaches 41°F within six hours.
No, the stew must cool to 70°F within two hours.
Yes, as long as the stew is stirred frequently.
No, the stew should have been placed directly in the freezer.
feedbacks: Incorrect: There is a two-stage cooling process.
Correct: The first stage of cooling requires that the food cool from 135°F to 70°F within two hours.
Incorrect: Stirring helps, but the temperature milestone must be met.
Incorrect: This is not a recommended cooling method.
questions.explanation: The two-stage cooling process requires that TCS food be cooled from 135°F to 70°F within two hours, and then from 70°F to 41°F or lower in the next four hours, for a total cooling time of six hours.

questions.question: A restaurant is holding a catered event at a park. What is the most important consideration for ensuring food safety at the off-site location?
answers: Having a variety of food choices for the guests.
Keeping hot food hot and cold food cold.
Having enough tables and chairs for all of the guests.
Decorating the food tables to look appealing.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While desirable, this is not a food safety issue.
Correct: Maintaining proper food temperatures is critical to prevent bacterial growth.
Incorrect: This is a logistical concern, not a food safety concern.
Incorrect: Aesthetics are secondary to food safety.
questions.explanation: When serving food at an off-site location, the most important food safety consideration is to maintain proper temperature control of all TCS foods. Hot food must be held at 135°F or higher, and cold food must be held at 41°F or lower.

questions.question: A manager notices that the sanitizer solution in the three-compartment sink is cloudy. What should they do?
answers: Add more sanitizer to the solution.
Test the solution with a test strip and adjust the concentration as needed.
Empty the sink and start over with a fresh solution.
Continue to use the solution as long as it still has a sanitizer smell.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This could make the solution too strong.
Correct: The concentration of the sanitizer should be checked regularly with a test strip.
Incorrect: While this is an option, testing the solution first is more efficient.
Incorrect: The smell of the sanitizer is not a reliable indicator of its concentration.
questions.explanation: The concentration of a sanitizer solution can be affected by factors such as food debris and temperature. It is important to test the solution regularly with a test strip to ensure it is at the proper concentration. If the solution is cloudy, it should be changed.

questions.question: Which of the following is a safe practice for storing food in a dry storage area?
answers: Storing food on the floor to keep it cool.
Keeping the storage area at a temperature of 85°F.
Storing food at least six inches off the floor and away from the walls.
Storing cleaning supplies on the same shelves as food.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Food should never be stored on the floor.
Incorrect: The ideal temperature for a dry storage area is between 50°F and 70°F.
Correct: This allows for proper air circulation and cleaning.
Incorrect: Cleaning supplies should be stored separately from food.
questions.explanation: Food in a dry storage area should be stored at least six inches off the floor and away from the walls to allow for air circulation and to prevent contamination.

questions.question: A food handler is preparing a dish that contains peanuts. A customer informs the server that they have a severe peanut allergy. What should the server do?
answers: multiple-choice
Incorrect: This is unprofessional and could escalate the situation.
Incorrect: While this may be done later, it's not the first priority.
Correct: The first step is to get the details of the situation.
Incorrect: This is a drastic step that may not be necessary.
feedbacks: Deny any responsibility for the illness.
Offer the customer a full refund.
Gather information from the customer, including their symptoms and what they ate.
Immediately close the restaurant.
questions.explanation: The manager should first listen to the customer, express concern, and gather as much information as possible, including contact information, symptoms, when they became ill, and what they ate. This information is crucial for an investigation.

questions.question: A food handler is using a single pair of gloves to assemble raw chicken skewers and then to plate a ready-to-eat salad. Which TWO food safety principles are being violated?
answers: Preventing cross-contamination
Practicing good personal hygiene
Controlling time and temperature
Using single-use gloves properly
Purchasing from approved, reputable suppliers
feedbacks: Correct: The gloves are transferring pathogens from the raw chicken to the salad.
Incorrect: While related, the primary violation is cross-contamination.
Incorrect: This scenario is not about time-temperature abuse.
Correct: Gloves are meant for a single task and should be changed between handling raw and ready-to-eat foods.
Incorrect: The source of the food is not the issue here.
questions.explanation: This action represents a classic case of cross-contamination. Single-use gloves are intended for one task only and must be changed when switching from raw to ready-to-eat foods to prevent the transfer of harmful pathogens.

questions.question: A restaurant's HACCP plan for grilled salmon identifies cooking as a critical control point (CCP). Which THREE elements are essential for the monitoring step of this CCP?
answers: The final internal temperature of the salmon.
The name of the employee cooking the salmon.
The time the salmon was on the grill.
The supplier of the salmon.
The date and time the temperature was taken.
The color of the salmon's exterior.
feedbacks: Correct: This is the critical limit that must be measured.
Incorrect: While good for traceability, it's not a core monitoring element of the CCP itself.
Correct: Time and temperature are both crucial for ensuring the salmon is cooked properly.
Incorrect: This is part of purchasing and receiving, not monitoring the cooking CCP.
Correct: Documentation of when the monitoring occurred is essential for verification.
Incorrect: Color is not a reliable indicator of doneness.
questions.explanation: Monitoring a CCP involves checking that the critical limits are being met. For cooked salmon, this means verifying it has reached the correct internal temperature (e.g., 145°F) for the specified time. Documenting the date and time of this check is also a key part of monitoring.

questions.question: A new walk-in refrigerator is being installed. To ensure food safety, which THREE features are most important?
answers: It must have an air temperature thermometer that is accurate to +/- 3°F.
The shelving should be made of a porous material like wood.
The unit should be placed on a smooth, nonabsorbent, and easy-to-clean floor.
There should be no air gap between the drainpipe and the floor drain.
The door should have a tight-fitting seal.
The lighting should be minimal to save energy.
feedbacks: Correct: Accurate temperature monitoring is crucial for food safety.
Incorrect: Shelving must be non-porous and easy to clean.
Correct: This prevents contamination and allows for proper sanitation.
Incorrect: An air gap is required to prevent backflow of contaminated water.
Correct: A good seal prevents warm air from entering and helps maintain a consistent temperature.
Incorrect: Adequate lighting is necessary for cleaning and inspecting food.
questions.explanation: A safe walk-in refrigerator must have an accurate thermometer, be on a floor that is easy to clean, and have a door that seals tightly to maintain the proper temperature. These features are essential for preventing foodborne illness.

questions.question: A food handler is diagnosed with Hepatitis A. Which TWO actions must the manager take?
answers: Allow the employee to work in a non-food handling position.
Report the diagnosis to the local regulatory authority.
Require the employee to wear gloves at all times.
Exclude the employee from the establishment.
Have the employee double-wash their hands every 30 minutes.
feedbacks: Incorrect: An employee with Hepatitis A must be excluded from the operation.
Correct: Hepatitis A is a highly contagious disease and must be reported.
Incorrect: Gloves are not sufficient to prevent the spread of Hepatitis A.
Correct: The employee must be excluded to prevent a foodborne illness outbreak.
Incorrect: While handwashing is important, it is not enough to prevent transmission from an infected individual.
questions.explanation: Hepatitis A is a serious, highly contagious virus. The manager has a legal responsibility to report the diagnosis to the local health department and to exclude the infected employee from the workplace to prevent an outbreak.

questions.question: A shipment of milk is delivered at 50°F. The delivery driver says it's fine because it was only in the truck for a short time. What TWO things should the receiving employee do?
answers: Accept the milk but cool it down immediately.
Take the temperature of the milk.
Ask the driver to sign a waiver of liability.
Reject the shipment of milk.
Move the milk to the front of the cooler to be used first.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The milk has already been in the temperature danger zone.
Correct: The employee should always verify the temperature of TCS foods upon delivery.
Incorrect: This does not make the food safe.
Correct: Cold TCS food must be received at 41°F or lower.
Incorrect: The milk should not be accepted in the first place.
questions.explanation: Cold TCS foods like milk must be received at 41°F or lower. A temperature of 50°F is in the temperature danger zone. The employee should verify the temperature and reject the shipment to ensure food safety.

questions.question: Which THREE of the following are considered acceptable methods for thawing frozen TCS food?
answers: On the countertop at room temperature.
In a microwave oven.
Under cold, running water.
In the refrigerator.
In a sink full of hot water.
In a warming drawer.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This allows the outer layers of the food to enter the temperature danger zone.
Correct: This is acceptable if the food is cooked immediately after thawing.
Correct: The water must be 70°F or lower, and the food should not be in the danger zone for more than 4 hours.
Correct: This is the safest method as it keeps the food out of the temperature danger zone.
Incorrect: Hot water will raise the food's temperature into the danger zone.
Incorrect: A warming drawer is for holding hot food, not for thawing.
questions.explanation: The three safe methods for thawing TCS food are in the refrigerator, in a microwave if cooked immediately, and under cold running water. These methods prevent the food from staying in the temperature danger zone for too long.

questions.question: A manager is training staff on cleaning and sanitizing. Which THREE of the following statements are correct?
answers: Sanitizing kills all microorganisms on a surface.
A surface must be cleaned before it can be sanitized.
The concentration of a sanitizer solution is not important.
Test strips should be used to check the sanitizer's strength.
Sanitizer works instantly on contact.
The water temperature can affect the effectiveness of a sanitizer.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Sanitizing reduces pathogens to safe levels; sterilization kills all microorganisms.
Correct: Cleaning removes food and dirt, allowing the sanitizer to work effectively.
Incorrect: The concentration must be correct to be effective and safe.
Correct: Test strips are the only way to ensure the sanitizer is at the proper concentration.
Incorrect: Sanitizers require a certain amount of contact time to be effective.
Correct: The manufacturer's instructions for the sanitizer will specify the correct water temperature.
questions.explanation: Proper cleaning and sanitizing requires that surfaces are first cleaned, then sanitized with a solution of the correct concentration, which should be verified with test strips. Water temperature is also a critical factor in the effectiveness of many sanitizers.

questions.question: An Integrated Pest Management (IPM) program has been implemented in a restaurant. Which THREE of the following are key components of this program?
answers: Applying pesticides throughout the facility on a weekly basis.
Working with a licensed Pest Control Operator (PCO).
Denying pests access to the building.
Storing food and supplies at least six inches off the floor.
Keeping the lights on in storage areas at all times.
Setting out open containers of bait in the kitchen.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Pesticides should be used sparingly and only when necessary by a licensed professional.
Correct: A PCO can provide expertise in identifying and controlling pests.
Correct: This includes sealing cracks and holes and using screens on windows and doors.
Correct: This eliminates hiding places for pests and makes it easier to clean.
Incorrect: While this might deter some pests, it is not a core component of an IPM program.
Incorrect: Bait should be placed in covered, tamper-resistant stations.
questions.explanation: An effective IPM program focuses on prevention. This includes denying pests access, denying them food and shelter (such as by storing items off the floor), and working with a licensed PCO for professional guidance and treatment when necessary.

questions.question: Which THREE of the following are considered major food allergens by the FDA?
answers: Wheat
Chocolate
Peanuts
Strawberries
Soybeans
Mustard
feedbacks: Correct: Wheat is one of the eight major food allergens.
Incorrect: While some people are allergic to chocolate, it is not one of the major allergens.
Correct: Peanuts are a major food allergen.
Incorrect: Strawberries are not one of the major allergens.
Correct: Soybeans are a major food allergen.
Incorrect: While mustard is a common allergen, it is not one of the eight major allergens in the US.
questions.explanation: The FDA has identified eight major food allergens that account for the majority of allergic reactions in the United States. These include wheat, peanuts, and soybeans, in addition to milk, eggs, fish, crustacean shellfish, and tree nuts.

questions.question: A food handler has been assigned to the dishwashing station. Which THREE of the following are part of their responsibilities for personal hygiene?
answers: Wearing a clean apron.
Washing hands frequently, especially after handling dirty dishes.
Wearing single-use gloves while operating the dish machine.
Keeping fingernails short and clean.
Tasting the food to make sure it's good.
Wearing a watch to keep track of time.
feedbacks: Correct: A clean apron helps prevent contamination.
Correct: Handwashing is crucial to prevent the spread of germs.
Incorrect: Gloves can be a hazard around a dish machine and are not a substitute for handwashing.
Correct: Long or dirty fingernails can harbor bacteria.
Incorrect: Food handlers should not eat, drink, or chew gum in the dishwashing area.
Incorrect: Jewelry, including watches, can harbor germs and should not be worn.
questions.explanation: Good personal hygiene for a dishwasher includes wearing clean clothing, washing hands frequently and properly, and maintaining clean fingernails. These practices help prevent the contamination of clean dishes.

questions.question: A restaurant serves a high-risk population. Which THREE of the following foods would be considered unsafe to serve to this group?
answers: A medium-rare steak
A salad with raw sprouts
A fully cooked chicken casserole
A smoothie made with pasteurized eggs
An omelet with a runny yolk
A baked potato
feedbacks: Correct: Undercooked meat poses a higher risk of foodborne illness.
Correct: Raw sprouts are a high-risk food due to the potential for bacterial contamination.
Incorrect: A thoroughly cooked casserole is generally safe.
Incorrect: Pasteurized eggs are safe to consume without cooking.
Correct: Undercooked eggs can contain Salmonella.
Incorrect: A fully cooked baked potato is a low-risk food.
questions.explanation: High-risk populations, such as the elderly, young children, and people with compromised immune systems, are more susceptible to foodborne illness. Therefore, they should not be served undercooked meats or eggs, or raw sprouts.

questions.question: A manager is setting up a dry storage area. Which THREE of the following are requirements for this area?
answers: The temperature should be between 50°F and 70°F.
The humidity should be kept high to prevent food from drying out.
There should be good air circulation.
Food should be stored in its original packaging whenever possible.
Food should be stored away from walls and at least six inches off the floor.
The area should be brightly lit with natural sunlight.
feedbacks: Correct: This is the ideal temperature range for dry storage.
Incorrect: Dry storage areas should have low humidity.
Correct: Good air circulation helps prevent the growth of mold and mildew.
Incorrect: Food should be stored in clean, covered containers.
Correct: This allows for cleaning and pest control.
Incorrect: Direct sunlight can damage some foods.
questions.explanation: A proper dry storage area should be cool, dry, and well-ventilated. Food should be stored off the floor and away from walls to allow for cleaning and to prevent pests.

questions.question: Which THREE of these are examples of a Critical Control Point (CCP) in a HACCP plan?
answers: Receiving a delivery of fresh produce.
Cooking a hamburger patty to a specific internal temperature.
Washing hands before handling food.
Cooling a large pot of chili.
Reheating a soup to the correct temperature before service.
Cleaning and sanitizing a cutting board.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While receiving is an important step, it is not always a CCP.
Correct: This is a CCP because it is the step that eliminates the hazard of bacteria.
Incorrect: Handwashing is a prerequisite program, not a CCP for a specific food.
Correct: This is a CCP because improper cooling can allow bacteria to grow.
Correct: This is a CCP to eliminate any bacteria that may have grown during storage.
Incorrect: This is a prerequisite program.
questions.explanation: A Critical Control Point (CCP) is a step in the flow of food where a hazard can be prevented, eliminated, or reduced to a safe level. Cooking, cooling, and reheating are common CCPs for many TCS foods.

questions.question: A food service operation has a power outage. Which THREE of the following actions should the manager take?
answers: Keep the refrigerator and freezer doors closed.
Start cooking all the food in the refrigerator immediately.
Note the time the power went out.
Use candles to light the kitchen.
Discard any TCS food that has been in the temperature danger zone for more than two hours.
Relocate all the food to a friend's restaurant.
feedbacks: Correct: This will help maintain the cold temperature for as long as possible.
Incorrect: This may not be possible or safe without power.
Correct: This is important for determining how long the food has been in the temperature danger zone.
Incorrect: Open flames can be a fire hazard.
Correct: This is a critical step to prevent foodborne illness.
Incorrect: This is not a practical or safe solution.
questions.explanation: During a power outage, the manager should take steps to minimize the impact on food safety. This includes keeping cold storage units closed, noting the time of the outage, and discarding any TCS food that has been in the temperature danger zone for too long.

questions.question: A server is taking an order from a customer with a known food allergy. Which THREE of the following actions should the server take?
answers: Tell the customer that the restaurant cannot accommodate their allergy.
Describe the dishes on the menu and how they are prepared.
Inform the kitchen staff about the customer's allergy.
Suggest dishes that do not contain the allergen.
Assume that the customer knows what they can and cannot eat.
Promise the customer that the dish will be 100% free of the allergen.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The restaurant should make every effort to accommodate the customer's needs.
Correct: This can help the customer identify potential allergens.
Correct: The kitchen staff needs to be aware of the allergy to prevent cross-contact.
Correct: This is a helpful and proactive way to assist the customer.
Incorrect: The server has a responsibility to help the customer make a safe choice.
Incorrect: It is better to be honest and explain the steps the restaurant will take to prevent cross-contact, without making an absolute guarantee.
questions.explanation: When a customer has a food allergy, the server should be knowledgeable about the menu, communicate the allergy to the kitchen, and help the customer choose a safe menu item.

questions.question: A restaurant is buying a new dishwasher. Which THREE of the following are important features for the dishwasher to have?
answers: The ability to reach a final rinse temperature of at least 180°F for a stationary rack machine.
A water pressure gauge.
A thermometer to measure the water temperature.
The ability to dispense the correct amount of sanitizer.
A self-cleaning cycle.
A quiet mode of operation.
feedbacks: Correct: This is the temperature required for hot water sanitizing.
Incorrect: While useful, a pressure gauge is not as critical as temperature and sanitizer concentration.
Correct: The dishwasher must have a way to verify that the water is reaching the correct sanitizing temperature.
Correct: For chemical sanitizing machines, the dispenser must be accurate.
Incorrect: While a convenience feature, it is not a primary food safety requirement.
Incorrect: The noise level of the dishwasher is not a food safety concern.
questions.explanation: A commercial dishwasher must be able to properly sanitize dishes, either with hot water or with a chemical sanitizer.
