This requires the machine to have a thermometer, a way to dispense the correct amount of sanitizer (if applicable), and the ability to reach the required temperatures.

questions.question: Which THREE of the following are symptoms that require a food handler to be excluded from the operation?
answers: A headache
Vomiting
Sore throat with fever
Jaundice
A runny nose
Itchy skin
feedbacks: Incorrect: A headache is not a symptom that requires exclusion unless it is accompanied by other symptoms.
Correct: Vomiting is a symptom of a foodborne illness and requires exclusion.
Correct: A sore throat with a fever requires exclusion, especially if the operation serves a high-risk population.
Correct: Jaundice is a symptom of Hepatitis A and requires exclusion and reporting to the health department.
Incorrect: A runny nose does not require exclusion, but the food handler should practice good hygiene.
Incorrect: Itchy skin is not a symptom that requires exclusion.
questions.explanation: Vomiting, a sore throat with a fever, and jaundice are all symptoms that require a food handler to be excluded from the operation to prevent the spread of foodborne illness.

questions.question: A manager is conducting an inspection of the dry storage area. Which THREE of the following would be cause for concern?
answers: Cans with bulging ends.
Boxes of pasta stored on a shelf 6 inches off the floor.
A bag of flour with a hole in it.
A case of sugar stored against a wall.
A box of crackers with a use-by date of yesterday.
A container of salt that is tightly sealed.
feedbacks: Correct: This can be a sign of botulism.
Incorrect: This is the correct way to store food.
Correct: This can allow pests and contaminants to enter the flour.
Incorrect: Food should be stored away from walls to allow for cleaning and pest control.
Correct: Expired food should be discarded.
Incorrect: This is the correct way to store salt.
questions.explanation: Bulging cans, damaged packaging, and expired food are all signs of potential food safety hazards and should be addressed immediately.

questions.question: Which THREE of the following are acceptable materials for food-contact surfaces?
answers: Copper
Stainless steel
Cast iron
Hardwood
Polyethylene
Non-toxic pewter
feedbacks: Incorrect: Copper can react with acidic foods and cause chemical contamination.
Correct: Stainless steel is non-porous, durable, and easy to clean.
Incorrect: Cast iron is porous and can be difficult to clean and sanitize.
Incorrect: Wood is absorbent and not recommended for food-contact surfaces.
Correct: Polyethylene (plastic) is a common and acceptable material for cutting boards and other food-contact surfaces.
Correct: Pewter that is non-toxic is an acceptable food-contact surface.
questions.explanation: Food-contact surfaces must be smooth, non-absorbent, and easy to clean. Stainless steel, polyethylene, and non-toxic pewter are all acceptable materials.

questions.question: A restaurant is serving a buffet. Which THREE of the following are important food safety practices for the buffet?
answers: Use sneeze guards to protect the food from contamination.
Provide a separate utensil for each food item.
Allow customers to bring their own containers to take food home.
Hold cold food at 45°F or below.
Check the temperature of the food at least every two hours.
Mix fresh food with food that has been on the buffet for a while.
feedbacks: Correct: Sneeze guards are a required physical barrier to protect food.
Correct: This prevents cross-contamination.
Incorrect: This can introduce outside contaminants.
Incorrect: Cold food must be held at 41°F or below.
Correct: Regular temperature monitoring is essential to ensure food safety.
Incorrect: This is not a safe practice.
questions.explanation: To ensure food safety at a buffet, it is important to use sneeze guards, provide separate utensils for each item, and monitor the temperature of the food regularly.

questions.question: A manager needs to create a master cleaning schedule. Which THREE pieces of information should be included for each task?
answers: Who is responsible for the task.
When the task should be done.
What should be cleaned.
The brand of cleaning supplies to be used.
The cost of the cleaning supplies.
The phone number of the cleaning supply company.
feedbacks: Correct: This ensures accountability.
Correct: This provides a clear schedule for cleaning.
Correct: The specific item or area to be cleaned must be identified.
Incorrect: While the type of cleaner is important, the specific brand is not necessary for the schedule.
Incorrect: This is a budgetary concern, not a part of the cleaning schedule itself.
Incorrect: This is not relevant to the master cleaning schedule.
questions.explanation: A master cleaning schedule should be a clear and comprehensive guide for the staff. It should include what needs to be cleaned, who is responsible for cleaning it, and when it should be cleaned.

questions.question: A food handler is preparing to start their shift. Which THREE of the following are required as part of good personal hygiene?
answers: Wearing a clean uniform.
Taking a shower before work.
Washing hands before handling food.
Wearing a hair restraint.
Wearing a watch with a leather band.
Chewing gum to keep their breath fresh.
feedbacks: Correct: Clean clothing helps prevent contamination.
Incorrect: While good personal hygiene is important, a shower is not a specific requirement of the food code.
Correct: Handwashing is the most important part of personal hygiene.
Correct: A hair restraint prevents hair from falling into food.
Incorrect: Watches and other jewelry should not be worn.
Incorrect: Eating, drinking, and chewing gum are not allowed in food preparation areas.
questions.explanation: Good personal hygiene for food handlers includes wearing clean clothing, washing hands properly and frequently, and wearing a hair restraint.

questions.question: Which THREE of the following are considered imminent health hazards that would require the immediate closure of a food service establishment?
answers: A power outage
A sewage backup
A broken piece of equipment
A foodborne illness outbreak
A shortage of staff
A customer complaint about slow service
feedbacks: Correct: A power outage can compromise refrigeration and cooking, creating a significant food safety risk.
Correct: A sewage backup can contaminate the entire facility.
Incorrect: A broken piece of equipment is not an imminent health hazard unless it directly affects food safety in a critical way.
Correct: A confirmed foodborne illness outbreak is a serious public health threat.
Incorrect: While a staffing shortage can be challenging, it is not an imminent health hazard.
Incorrect: This is a service issue, not a health hazard.
questions.explanation: An imminent health hazard is a situation that creates a significant threat of contamination, illness, or injury and requires immediate correction or closure. Power outages, sewage backups, and foodborne illness outbreaks are all examples of imminent health hazards.

questions.question: A restaurant is receiving a delivery of frozen shrimp. Which THREE of the following would be reasons to reject the shipment?
answers: The shrimp are frozen solid.
There are large ice crystals on the shrimp.
The packaging is torn.
The temperature of the shrimp is 0°F.
The shrimp has a use-by date that is two weeks away.
The shrimp has a soft, mushy texture.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is the desired state for frozen shrimp.
Correct: This can be a sign that the shrimp has been thawed and refrozen.
Correct: Damaged packaging can expose the shrimp to contamination.
Incorrect: This is a safe temperature for frozen food.
Incorrect: This is an acceptable use-by date.
Correct: This is a sign of spoilage.
questions.explanation: Frozen food should be rejected if there are signs of thawing and refreezing, such as large ice crystals, or if the packaging is damaged. A soft, mushy texture is also a sign of spoilage.

questions.question: A manager is developing a food allergy awareness program for the staff. Which THREE of the following should be included in the training?
answers: The eight major food allergens.
How to prevent cross-contact.
What to do in case of an allergic reaction.
How to diagnose a food allergy.
The cost of allergy-friendly menu items.
The history of food allergies.
feedbacks: Correct: The staff should be able to identify the most common food allergens.
Correct: This is a critical skill for preventing allergic reactions.
Correct: The staff should know how to respond to an emergency.
Incorrect: The staff should not be diagnosing allergies; this is the responsibility of a medical professional.
Incorrect: This is a pricing issue, not a food safety issue.
Incorrect: While interesting, this is not essential information for the staff.
questions.explanation: A food allergy awareness program should focus on practical information that will help the staff prevent and respond to allergic reactions. This includes knowing the major allergens, how to prevent cross-contact, and what to do in an emergency.

questions.question: A restaurant is installing a new ventilation system in the kitchen. Which THREE of the following are important functions of this system?
answers: To remove heat from the kitchen.
To remove grease from the air.
To provide fresh air to the kitchen.
To make the kitchen quieter.
To provide a place to store cleaning supplies.
To cool the food quickly.
feedbacks: Correct: A ventilation system helps to keep the kitchen cool and comfortable.
Correct: This helps to prevent fires.
Correct: Good ventilation improves air quality for the staff.
Incorrect: A ventilation system can be noisy.
Incorrect: The ventilation system should not be used for storage.
Incorrect: A ventilation system is not a substitute for proper cooling methods.
questions.explanation: A kitchen ventilation system is important for removing heat, smoke, grease, and odors from the kitchen. It also provides fresh air, which improves the working environment for the staff.

questions.question: Which THREE of the following are acceptable ways to cool hot food?
answers: Place the food in an ice-water bath.
Divide the food into smaller containers.
Stir the food with an ice paddle.
Place the food on the counter to cool overnight.
Place the food directly into the freezer.
Add a large block of ice to the food.
feedbacks: Correct: An ice-water bath is a fast and effective way to cool food.
Correct: Smaller portions cool faster than large portions.
Correct: An ice paddle is a tool specifically designed for cooling food quickly.
Incorrect: This allows the food to remain in the temperature danger zone for too long.
Incorrect: This can raise the temperature of the freezer and put other foods at risk.
Incorrect: This can dilute the food and may not cool it evenly.
questions.explanation: The goal of cooling is to get the food through the temperature danger zone as quickly as possible. Using an ice-water bath, dividing the food into smaller portions, and using an ice paddle are all effective methods for rapid cooling.

questions.question: A manager is doing a walk-through of the kitchen and observes several food safety violations. Which THREE of the following require immediate corrective action?
answers: A food handler is not wearing a hair restraint.
A box of single-use gloves is stored on the floor.
The handwashing sink is being used to store dirty dishes.
The exhaust hood has a small amount of grease on it.
A food handler is chewing gum while prepping food.
The menu board has a spelling error.
feedbacks: Correct: This is a violation that could lead to physical contamination and should be corrected immediately.
Correct: Storing items on the floor is a violation and can lead to contamination.
Correct: The handwashing sink must be accessible at all times and should never be used for other purposes.
Incorrect: While this should be cleaned, it is not an immediate threat to food safety.
Incorrect: While this is a violation, it is not as critical as the others.
Incorrect: This is not a food safety issue.
questions.explanation: A food handler without a hair restraint, items stored on the floor, and a blocked handwashing sink are all violations that pose an immediate risk to food safety and require immediate corrective action.

questions.question: A restaurant has a policy that all TCS food must be labeled with the date it was prepared. Which THREE pieces of information should be on the label?
answers: The name of the food.
The date the food was prepared.
The use-by date.
The name of the employee who prepared the food.
The cost of the food.
The recipe for the food.
feedbacks: Correct: This identifies the contents of the container.
Correct: This is essential for tracking the shelf life of the food.
Correct: This tells the staff when the food must be used or discarded.
Incorrect: While this can be helpful for traceability, it is not a requirement for the label.
Incorrect: This is not a food safety requirement.
Incorrect: The recipe is not needed on the label.
questions.explanation: A proper date-marking label for TCS food should include the name of the food, the date it was prepared, and the use-by date. This helps to ensure that the food is used within its safe shelf life.

questions.question: Which THREE of the following are potential sources of chemical contamination in a food service operation?
answers: Pesticides
Sanitizers
Polishes
Bacteria
Viruses
Parasites
feedbacks: Correct: Pesticides can be a source of chemical contamination if they are not used properly.
Correct: Sanitizers can be a source of chemical contamination if they are not used at the correct concentration or if they are accidentally mixed with food.
Correct: Polishes and other cleaning products can be a source of chemical contamination.
Incorrect: Bacteria are a biological contaminant.
Incorrect: Viruses are a biological contaminant.
Incorrect: Parasites are a biological contaminant.
questions.explanation: Chemical contaminants are substances such as pesticides, sanitizers, and polishes that can cause illness if they get into food. It is important to store and use these chemicals properly to prevent contamination.

questions.question: A manager is training a new employee on how to use a thermometer. Which THREE of the following are important steps in this process?
answers: Calibrate the thermometer regularly.
Insert the thermometer into the thickest part of the food.
Wait for the thermometer reading to steady before recording the temperature.
Use the same thermometer for raw and cooked food without cleaning it.
Store the thermometer in a drawer with other utensils.
Guess the temperature if the thermometer is not working.
feedbacks: Correct: A thermometer must be calibrated to ensure it is accurate.
Correct: This gives the most accurate reading of the internal temperature.
Correct: The thermometer needs time to register the correct temperature.
Incorrect: This can cause cross-contamination.
Incorrect: The thermometer should be stored in a clean, protective case.
Incorrect: An accurate temperature reading is essential for food safety.
questions.explanation: To get an accurate temperature reading, it is important to use a calibrated thermometer, insert it into the thickest part of the food, and wait for the reading to steady.

questions.question: A restaurant is serving a special event and is using time as a public health control. Which THREE of the following are requirements for this practice?
answers: The food must be labeled with the time it was removed from temperature control.
The food must be thrown out after four hours.
The food must be cooked to a higher temperature than usual.
The food must be held at 41°F or below before it is removed from temperature control.
The food can be returned to the refrigerator after the event is over.
The food does not need to be monitored during the event.
feedbacks: Correct: This is essential for tracking the four-hour time limit.
Correct: This is the maximum amount of time that TCS food can be held without temperature control.
Incorrect: The cooking temperature is not affected by the use of time as a public health control.
Correct: The food must start at a safe temperature.
Incorrect: Once time is used as a control, the food cannot be re-chilled and served later.
Incorrect: The food should be monitored to ensure it is discarded after four hours.
questions.explanation: When using time as a public health control, the food must start at a safe temperature, be labeled with the time it was removed from temperature control, and be discarded after four hours.

questions.question: A food handler is not feeling well but wants to work. Which THREE of the following symptoms would require the food handler to stay home from work?
answers: A persistent cough
Diarrhea
A sore throat with a fever
Vomiting
A stuffy nose
A paper cut on a finger
feedbacks: Incorrect: While a cough can be a sign of illness, it does not require exclusion unless it is accompanied by other symptoms.
Correct: Diarrhea is a symptom of a foodborne illness and requires exclusion.
Correct: A sore throat with a fever requires exclusion.
Correct: Vomiting is a symptom of a foodborne illness and requires exclusion.
Incorrect: A stuffy nose is not a symptom that requires exclusion.
Incorrect: A paper cut can be covered with a bandage and a glove.
questions.explanation: Diarrhea, a sore throat with a fever, and vomiting are all symptoms that require a food handler to be excluded from the operation to prevent the spread of foodborne illness.

questions.question: A restaurant is cleaning its grease trap. Which THREE of the following are important considerations for this task?
answers: The grease trap should be cleaned regularly to prevent backups.
The grease should be disposed of in a designated container, not down the drain.
The person cleaning the grease trap should wear personal protective equipment.
The grease trap can be cleaned while the restaurant is in operation.
The grease from the trap can be used for cooking.
The grease trap only needs to be cleaned once a year.
feedbacks: Correct: Regular cleaning is essential for the proper functioning of the grease trap.
Correct: Disposing of grease down the drain can cause plumbing problems.
Correct: Cleaning a grease trap can be a dirty and hazardous job.
Incorrect: It is best to clean the grease trap when the restaurant is closed to minimize disruption.
Incorrect: The grease from a grease trap is waste and should not be used for cooking.
Incorrect: The frequency of cleaning depends on the size of the grease trap and the volume of business.
questions.explanation: Grease traps should be cleaned regularly by a trained professional. The grease should be disposed of properly, and the person cleaning the trap should wear personal protective equipment.

questions.question: Which THREE of the following are examples of physical contaminants that can be found in food?
answers: A piece of glass
A metal shaving from a can opener
A bandage
Mold on a piece of cheese
Sanitizer in a glass of water
Toxins produced by fish
feedbacks: Correct: Glass is a physical contaminant that can cause serious injury.
Correct: Metal shavings are a common physical contaminant.
Correct: A bandage is a physical contaminant that can fall into food.
Incorrect: Mold is a biological contaminant.
Incorrect: Sanitizer is a chemical contaminant.
Incorrect: Fish toxins are a biological contaminant.
questions.explanation: Physical contaminants are foreign objects that can get into food. Glass, metal shavings, and bandages are all examples of physical contaminants.

questions.question: A manager is training employees on how to safely store food in the cooler. Which THREE of the following are correct procedures?
answers: Store raw poultry on the top shelf.
Keep the cooler temperature at 41°F or below.
Cover all food with a tight-fitting lid or plastic wrap.
Store ready-to-eat food below raw meat.
Leave the cooler door open to improve air circulation.
Store food in its original cardboard shipping boxes.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Raw poultry should be stored on the bottom shelf to prevent it from dripping onto other foods.
Correct: This is the required temperature for cold food storage.
Correct: This helps to prevent cross-contamination.
Incorrect: Ready-to-eat food should be stored above raw meat.
Incorrect: The cooler door should be kept closed as much as possible to maintain the temperature.
Incorrect: Cardboard boxes can harbor pests and should be discarded.
questions.explanation: To safely store food in a cooler, the temperature should be kept at 41°F or below, all food should be covered, and food should be stored in the correct top-to-bottom order to prevent cross-contamination. Removing food from its original cardboard box is also a good practice.

questions.question: A restaurant has a pest problem. Which THREE of the following are signs of a rodent infestation?
answers: Gnaw marks on food packages
Droppings that are shiny and black
Nests made of shredded paper and cloth
A strong, oily odor
Capsule-shaped egg cases
Flies buzzing around the garbage cans
feedbacks: Correct: Rodents gnaw on things to keep their teeth sharp.
Correct: Rodent droppings are a sure sign of an infestation.
Correct: Rodents build nests in quiet, dark places.
Incorrect: This is a sign of a cockroach infestation.
Incorrect: This is a sign of a cockroach infestation.
Incorrect: While flies are a pest, they are not a sign of a rodent infestation.
questions.explanation: Signs of a rodent infestation include gnaw marks, droppings, and nests. If you see any of these signs, you should contact a licensed pest control operator immediately.

questions.question: Which THREE of the following are the responsibility of the Person in Charge (PIC) of a food service establishment?
answers: Ensuring that all employees are trained in food safety.
Monitoring the health of employees to prevent the spread of illness.
Demonstrating knowledge of foodborne disease prevention.
Cooking all of the food in the restaurant.
Taking out the garbage at the end of the night.
Greeting all of the customers at the door.
feedbacks: Correct: The PIC is responsible for the training of all employees.
Correct: The PIC must ensure that sick employees do not handle food.
Correct: The PIC must be able to answer questions about food safety from the health inspector.
Incorrect: The PIC is a manager, not necessarily a cook.
Incorrect: The PIC may delegate this task to other employees.
Incorrect: While good for business, this is not a food safety responsibility.
questions.explanation: The Person in Charge (PIC) is responsible for ensuring that the establishment is in compliance with all food safety regulations. This includes training employees, monitoring their health, and being able to demonstrate knowledge of food safety principles.

questions.question: A restaurant is preparing to close for the night. Which THREE of the following are important cleaning and sanitizing tasks that should be done daily?
answers: Clean and sanitize all food-contact surfaces.
Sweep and mop the floors.
Empty the garbage cans.
Clean the grease trap.
Wash the windows.
Organize the dry storage area.
feedbacks: Correct: This is essential to prevent the growth of bacteria overnight.
Correct: This removes dirt and debris that can attract pests.
Correct: This prevents odors and pests.
Incorrect: The grease trap does not need to be cleaned daily.
Incorrect: The windows do not need to be washed daily.
Incorrect: While a good practice, this is not a cleaning and sanitizing task.
questions.explanation: Daily cleaning and sanitizing tasks should focus on areas that are most likely to harbor bacteria or attract pests. This includes food-contact surfaces, floors, and garbage cans.

questions.question: A food handler is making a batch of soup. They take the temperature of the soup and it is 145°F. They continue to cook the soup for another 15 minutes. Is the soup safe to serve?
answers: Yes, because it was cooked for a long time.
No, because it did not reach the correct temperature.
Yes, because it is above the hot-holding temperature of 135°F.
No, because it was not stirred while it was cooking.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The final temperature is what matters most.
Correct: Soup, which is a TCS food, must be cooked to a minimum internal temperature of 165°F.
Incorrect: The cooking temperature is different from the hot-holding temperature.
Incorrect: While stirring is a good practice, the main issue is the temperature.
questions.explanation: Soup is a TCS food that must be cooked to a minimum internal temperature of 165°F for 15 seconds to be safe to eat. A temperature of 145°F is not sufficient.

questions.question: A restaurant is having a problem with flies in the kitchen. Which of the following is the BEST long-term solution to this problem?
answers: Installing an air curtain at the back door.
Hanging flypaper from the ceiling.
Spraying insecticide in the kitchen every morning.
Keeping the back door closed.
feedbacks: Correct: An air curtain creates a barrier of air that prevents flies from entering.
Incorrect: Flypaper is a temporary solution and can be a source of contamination if it is not used properly.
Incorrect: Insecticides should be used as a last resort and applied by a licensed professional.
Incorrect: While helpful, it is not always practical to keep the door closed, especially during deliveries.
questions.explanation: An air curtain is a device that blows a steady stream of air across an open doorway. This creates a barrier that is difficult for flies and other flying insects to penetrate. It is a more effective and long-term solution than flypaper or insecticides.

questions.question: Which of the following is a safe way to handle a customer's request for an allergen-free meal?
answers: Tell the customer that you cannot guarantee that the meal will be allergen-free.
Prepare the allergen-free meal in a separate area of the kitchen with clean and sanitized utensils.
Cook the allergen-free meal on the same grill as other foods, but in a different spot.
Ask the customer to sign a waiver releasing the restaurant from liability.
feedbacks: Incorrect: While you should be honest about the risks of cross-contact, you should also take steps to prepare the meal safely.
Correct: This is the best way to prevent cross-contact.
Incorrect: This does not prevent cross-contact from airborne particles or shared utensils.
Incorrect: This is not a substitute for taking proper food safety precautions.
questions.explanation: To prevent cross-contact, it is essential to prepare allergen-free meals in a separate area of the kitchen with dedicated equipment and utensils that have been thoroughly cleaned and sanitized.

questions.question: A food handler is washing their hands. What is the minimum amount of time they should scrub their hands with soap?
answers: 5 seconds
10-15 seconds
20 seconds
30 seconds
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is not long enough to remove all of the germs.
Correct: The entire handwashing process should take about 20 seconds, with 10-15 seconds of that time devoted to scrubbing.
Incorrect: The entire process should take 20 seconds, but the scrubbing portion is shorter.
Incorrect: This is longer than necessary.
questions.explanation: The FDA Food Code recommends that food handlers scrub their hands with soap for at least 10-15 seconds as part of the 20-second handwashing process.

questions.question: A restaurant has been without power for four hours. The manager checks the temperature of the food in the walk-in cooler and it is 50°F. What should the manager do with the TCS food?
answers: Cook it and serve it immediately.
Donate it to a local food bank.
Discard it.
Wait for the power to come back on and then cool it down.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The food has been in the temperature danger zone for too long.
Incorrect: The food is not safe to eat and should not be donated.
Correct: The food has been in the temperature danger zone for more than four hours and is no longer safe to eat.
Incorrect: The food has already been at an unsafe temperature for too long.
questions.explanation: TCS food that has been in the temperature danger zone (41°F to 135°F) for four hours or more must be discarded.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of a corrective action in a HACCP plan?
answers: Taking the temperature of a food.
Discarding a food that has not been cooked to the proper temperature.
Washing your hands before handling food.
Calibrating a thermometer.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is a monitoring step.
Correct: A corrective action is taken when a critical limit has not been met.
Incorrect: This is a prerequisite program.
Incorrect: This is a verification step.
questions.explanation: A corrective action is a step that is taken to correct a problem that has occurred in the flow of food. Discarding a food that has not reached its minimum internal cooking temperature is an example of a corrective action.

questions.question: A restaurant is storing chemicals in the dry storage area. Which of the following is a safe practice for storing these chemicals?
answers: Store them on the top shelf to prevent them from dripping onto food.
Store them in their original containers with the labels clearly visible.
Store them in unmarked spray bottles for easy access.
Store them next to the food to save space.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Chemicals should be stored below and away from food.
Correct: This helps to prevent accidental misuse.
Incorrect: All chemical containers must be clearly labeled.
Incorrect: Chemicals should be stored in a separate area from food.
questions.explanation: Chemicals should be stored in a designated area away from food and food-contact surfaces. They should be kept in their original containers with the labels intact to prevent accidental poisoning.

questions.question: A food handler has a sore throat and a fever. They work in a restaurant that serves a general population. What should the manager do?
answers: Restrict the food handler from working with or around food.
Exclude the food handler from the operation.
Allow the food handler to work as long as they wear a mask.
Send the food handler home without pay.
feedbacks: Correct: A food handler with a sore throat and fever should be restricted from working with food.
Incorrect: Exclusion is only required if the operation serves a high-risk population.
Incorrect: A mask is not sufficient to prevent the spread of illness.
Incorrect: The manager should follow the restaurant's sick leave policy.
questions.explanation: A food handler with a sore throat and fever who works in an operation that serves a general population should be restricted from working with or around food. They can be given other tasks, such as cleaning restrooms or taking out the trash.

questions.question: What is the best way to prevent backflow in a food service establishment?
answers: Install a grease trap.
Create an air gap between the faucet and the sink.
Use a water filter.
Increase the water pressure.
feedbacks: Incorrect: A grease trap is used to prevent grease from entering the sewer system.
Correct: An air gap is the most reliable way to prevent backflow.
Incorrect: A water filter removes impurities from the water, but it does not prevent backflow.
Incorrect: This can actually make backflow more likely.
questions.explanation: An air gap is a physical separation between the end of a faucet and the flood rim of a sink. This separation prevents contaminated water from being siphoned back into the clean water supply.

questions.question: A restaurant is using a time-temperature indicator (TTI) on a shipment of fresh fish. What is the purpose of a TTI?
answers: To measure the exact temperature of the fish.
To show if the fish has been time-temperature abused during shipment.
To indicate the age of the fish.
To prove that the fish is from a reputable supplier.
feedbacks: Incorrect: A TTI does not give a specific temperature reading.
Correct: A TTI is a device that changes color if the food has been exposed to unsafe temperatures for too long.
Incorrect: The TTI does not indicate the age of the fish.
Incorrect: A TTI does not provide information about the supplier.
questions.explanation: A time-temperature indicator (TTI) is a tool that can be used to monitor the temperature of a food product during transportation and storage. It provides a visual indication if the product has been subjected to time-temperature abuse.

questions.question: Which of the following is a safe practice for serving food to customers?
answers: Use your bare hands to place a roll on a customer's plate.
Use the same utensil to serve mashed potatoes and green beans.
Hold a plate by the bottom and edge.
Carry a glass by putting your fingers inside the rim.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Bare-hand contact with ready-to-eat food is not allowed.
Incorrect: A separate utensil should be used for each food item to prevent cross-contamination.
Correct: This prevents your fingers from touching the food.
Incorrect: This can contaminate the glass.
questions.explanation: When serving food, it is important to avoid touching the food or the food-contact surfaces of plates and glassware. Holding a plate by the bottom and edge is the proper way to carry it.

questions.question: A manager is checking the temperature of food in a hot-holding unit. The temperature of the food is 130°F. What should the manager do?
answers: Leave the food in the hot-holding unit and check it again in an hour.
Reheat the food to 165°F and then return it to the hot-holding unit.
Discard the food.
Add hot water to the food to raise the temperature.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The food is already in the temperature danger zone.
Correct: If the food has been in the temperature danger zone for less than two hours, it can be reheated to 165°F.
Incorrect: The food can be saved if it is reheated properly.
Incorrect: This is not a safe way to reheat food.
questions.explanation: Hot TCS food must be held at 135°F or higher. If the temperature of the food falls into the temperature danger zone, it must be reheated to 165°F for 15 seconds before it can be served.

questions.question: A restaurant is receiving a delivery of food. Which of the following is a reason to reject a shipment of fresh poultry?
answers: The poultry is firm to the touch.
The poultry has a purple or greenish discoloration.
The poultry is surrounded by crushed, self-draining ice.
The temperature of the poultry is 41°F.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is a sign of good quality poultry.
Correct: This is a sign of spoilage.
Incorrect: This is the proper way to pack fresh poultry.
Incorrect: This is the maximum acceptable temperature for fresh poultry.
questions.explanation: Fresh poultry should have a pinkish color and be firm to the touch. A purple or greenish discoloration is a sign of spoilage, and the shipment should be rejected.

questions.question: A food handler has been diagnosed with Shigellosis. What should the manager do?
answers: Allow the food handler to work as long as they wash their hands frequently.
Exclude the food handler from the operation.
Assign the food handler to a non-food handling position.
Tell the food handler to take antibiotics and return to work in a few days.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Shigellosis is a highly contagious disease, and the employee must be excluded.
Correct: The FDA Food Code requires that employees with a diagnosis of Shigellosis be excluded from the establishment.
Incorrect: The risk of transmission is too high.
Incorrect: The manager must exclude the employee and should not be giving medical advice.
questions.explanation: Shigellosis is a foodborne illness that is easily transmitted from person to person. An employee who has been diagnosed with Shigellosis must be excluded from the food service operation to prevent an outbreak.

questions.question: What is the most important factor to consider when choosing a food supplier?
answers: The supplier has the lowest prices.
The supplier is located close to the restaurant.
The supplier has been inspected and is in compliance with all applicable laws and regulations.
The supplier offers a wide variety of products.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The price of the food is not as important as its safety.
Incorrect: The location of the supplier is not a primary concern.
Correct: A food supplier should be able to show you their inspection report.
Incorrect: The variety of products is not as important as their safety.
questions.explanation: A food service establishment should only purchase food from suppliers who are approved and have been inspected by the appropriate regulatory authorities. This helps to ensure that the food is safe and has been handled properly throughout the supply chain.

questions.question: A restaurant is using a chemical sanitizer in a three-compartment sink. What is the minimum temperature of the water in the sanitizing compartment?
feedbacks: Correct: The water temperature for chemical sanitizing should be at least 75°F, unless the sanitizer manufacturer's instructions state otherwise.
Incorrect: This is the temperature for the wash compartment.
Incorrect: This is the temperature for hot water sanitizing.
Incorrect: This is the boiling point of water.
questions.explanation: When using a chemical sanitizer, the water temperature in the third compartment of a three-compartment sink should be at least 75°F to ensure that the sanitizer is effective.

questions.question: A food handler is preparing to cater an outdoor event. They are packing a cooler with cold TCS food. What should they do to ensure the food stays cold?
answers: Pack the food loosely to allow for air circulation.
Pack the food in a single layer at the bottom of the cooler.
Pack the cooler with as much ice as possible.
Place the cooler in the trunk of the car where it will be dark.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The food should be packed tightly to help it stay cold.
Incorrect: The food should be packed in layers with ice or gel packs in between.
Correct: The more ice, the longer the food will stay cold.
Incorrect: The trunk of a car can get very hot, even on a cool day.
questions.explanation: To keep food cold in a cooler, it is important to use plenty of ice or gel packs. The food should be packed tightly, and the cooler should be kept in a cool, shaded place.

questions.question: Which of the following is a common symptom of a food allergy?
answers: Hives
A fever
Jaundice
Diarrhea
feedbacks: Correct: Hives are a common skin reaction to a food allergen.
Incorrect: A fever is more likely to be a symptom of a foodborne illness.
Incorrect: Jaundice is a symptom of Hepatitis A.
Incorrect: Diarrhea can be a symptom of a food allergy, but it is also a common symptom of a foodborne illness.
questions.explanation: The symptoms of a food allergy can range from mild to severe and can include hives, itching, swelling, difficulty breathing, and abdominal pain.

questions.question: A restaurant is installing a new handwashing station. Which of the following is NOT a requirement for a handwashing station?
answers: A sign that tells employees to wash their hands.
Hot and cold running water.
Soap.
A way to dry hands.
feedbacks: Correct: While it is a good idea to have a sign, it is not a requirement of the food code.
Incorrect: A handwashing station must have both hot and cold running water.
Incorrect: Soap is a requirement for a handwashing station.
Incorrect: A handwashing station must have a way to dry hands, such as single-use paper towels or a hand dryer.
questions.explanation: While a handwashing sign is a good reminder for employees, it is not a requirement of the FDA Food Code. The other three items are all required components of a handwashing station.

questions.question: A manager is training a new employee on the proper way to cool food. They explain that the food must be cooled from 135°F to 70°F within two hours, and then from 70°F to 41°F or lower in the next four hours. What is this method of cooling called?
answers: The one-stage cooling method.
The two-stage cooling method.
The rapid cooling method.
The slow cooling method.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is not a recognized term.
Correct: This is the FDA-approved method for cooling TCS food.
Incorrect: While the goal is to cool the food rapidly, the specific method is called the two-stage method.
Incorrect: Slow cooling is not a safe method for cooling food.
questions.explanation: The FDA Food Code requires that TCS food be cooled using the two-stage cooling method. This method is designed to get the food through the temperature danger zone as quickly as possible.

questions.question: A restaurant has a problem with cockroaches. Where are the cockroaches most likely to be found?
answers: In bright, open areas.
In dark, warm, and moist places.
In cold, dry places.
In the dining room where there is plenty of food.
feedbacks: Incorrect: Cockroaches prefer dark, warm, and moist places.
Correct: Cockroaches are attracted to these conditions.
Incorrect: Cockroaches do not like cold, dry places.
Incorrect: Cockroaches prefer to hide in cracks and crevices, not out in the open.
questions.explanation: Cockroaches are nocturnal insects that prefer to live in dark, warm, and moist places. They are often found in cracks and crevices, behind equipment, and in drains.

questions.question: Which of the following is a safe way to store raw meat in a refrigerator?
answers: On the top shelf, above ready-to-eat food.
On a plate, uncovered.
On the bottom shelf, below ready-to-eat food.
Next to the vegetables.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This can cause cross-contamination.
Incorrect: Raw meat should always be covered to prevent it from dripping onto other foods.
Correct: This prevents raw meat juices from dripping onto and contaminating other foods.
Incorrect: This can cause cross-contamination.
questions.explanation: To prevent cross-contamination, raw meat should be stored on the bottom shelf of the refrigerator, below ready-to-eat food.

questions.question: A food handler is wearing a plain metal wedding band. Is this a violation of food safety regulations?
answers: Yes, all jewelry is prohibited in the kitchen.
No, a plain wedding band is the only piece of jewelry that is allowed to be worn.
Yes, unless the food handler is wearing gloves.
No, as long as the food handler washes their hands frequently.
feedbacks: Incorrect: A plain band is often the only exception.
Correct: Most jurisdictions allow food handlers to wear a plain, smooth wedding band.
Incorrect: The ring itself is the issue, not whether gloves are worn.
Incorrect: Handwashing does not negate the rule about jewelry.
questions.explanation: The FDA Food Code allows food handlers to wear a plain wedding band. Other types of jewelry, such as watches, bracelets, and rings with stones, are not allowed because they can harbor bacteria and are difficult to clean.

questions.question: A restaurant is holding a buffet. How often should the temperature of the food on the buffet be checked?
answers: Once, at the beginning of the buffet.
Every hour.
Every two hours.
Every four hours.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The temperature needs to be checked regularly.
Incorrect: While frequent checking is good, the requirement is less strict.
Correct: The temperature of food on a buffet should be checked at least every two hours to ensure it is being held at the proper temperature.
Incorrect: This is too long between checks. If a problem is found, the food may have been in the danger zone for too long.
questions.explanation: To ensure that food on a buffet is being held at a safe temperature, it should be checked at least every two hours. This allows for corrective action to be taken if the temperature has fallen into the temperature danger zone.

questions.question: A restaurant is using a new type of chemical sanitizer. What is the best way for the manager to ensure that the sanitizer is being used correctly?
answers: Ask the employees if they think the sanitizer is working.
Follow the manufacturer's instructions for the sanitizer.
Use the same concentration as the old sanitizer.
Smell the sanitizer to make sure it is strong enough.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The employees' opinion is not a reliable measure of the sanitizer's effectiveness.
Correct: The manufacturer's instructions will provide specific information on how to use the sanitizer safely and effectively.
Incorrect: Different sanitizers may have different concentration requirements.
Incorrect: The smell of the sanitizer is not a reliable indicator of its strength.
questions.explanation: The most important thing to do when using a new chemical sanitizer is to read and follow the manufacturer's instructions. This will ensure that the sanitizer is used at the correct concentration and contact time to be effective.

questions.question: A food handler has been diagnosed with Norovirus. When can they return to work?
answers: After they have been symptom-free for 24 hours.
After they have taken a full course of antibiotics.
After they have a written release from their doctor.
After they have passed a stool test.
feedbacks: Correct: The FDA Food Code requires that an employee with Norovirus be symptom-free for at least 24 hours before returning to work.
Incorrect: Antibiotics are not effective against viruses.
Incorrect: While a doctor's note may be required by the employer, the minimum standard is being symptom-free for 24 hours.
Incorrect: This is not a standard requirement.
questions.explanation: An employee who has been diagnosed with Norovirus must be excluded from the operation and cannot return to work until they have been symptom-free for at least 24 hours.

questions.question: Which of the following is a requirement for a food-contact surface?
answers: It must be made of a dark color to hide dirt.
It must be smooth and easy to clean.
It must be able to withstand high temperatures.
It must be disposable so that it can be thrown away after each use.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The color of the surface is not important.
Correct: A food-contact surface must be non-absorbent, smooth, and easy to clean and sanitize.
Incorrect: While some food-contact surfaces need to be heat-resistant, this is not a requirement for all of them.
Incorrect: Food-contact surfaces can be reusable as long as they are properly cleaned and sanitized.
questions.explanation: A food-contact surface is any surface that comes into direct contact with food. These surfaces must be smooth, non-absorbent, and easy to clean and sanitize to prevent the growth of bacteria.

questions.question: A restaurant is storing raw ground beef and whole cuts of beef in a cooler. What is the correct top-to-bottom storage order?
answers: Ground beef, whole cuts of beef.
Whole cuts of beef, ground beef.
The order does not matter as long as they are on separate shelves.
They can be stored on the same shelf as long as they are in separate containers.
feedbacks: Incorrect: This order increases the risk of cross-contamination.
Correct: Whole cuts of beef should be stored above ground beef.
Incorrect: The storage order is important to prevent cross-contamination.
Incorrect: They should be on separate shelves.
questions.explanation: To prevent cross-contamination, food should be stored in the cooler in order of its minimum internal cooking temperature. Whole cuts of beef have a lower cooking temperature than ground beef, so they should be stored above the ground beef.

questions.question: A restaurant is holding a catered event. They are transporting hot food to the event site. What is the minimum temperature at which the food should be held during transport?
feedbacks: Incorrect: This is in the temperature danger zone.
Correct: Hot TCS food must be held at 135°F or higher.
Incorrect: This is higher than the minimum requirement.
Incorrect: This is the reheating temperature, not the hot-holding temperature.
questions.explanation: Hot TCS food must be held at an internal temperature of 135°F or higher during transport to prevent the growth of bacteria.

questions.question: A food handler is cleaning up a spill in the kitchen. What is the first thing they should do?
answers: Pour bleach on the spill to sanitize it.
Put a "wet floor" sign over the spill.
Wipe up the spill with a cloth towel.
Get a mop and bucket.
feedbacks: Incorrect: The spill should be cleaned up before it is sanitized.
Correct: This is the first step to prevent anyone from slipping and falling.
Incorrect: A cloth towel can spread the spill around.
Incorrect: While a mop and bucket will be needed, the first step is to warn others of the hazard.
questions.explanation: The first thing to do when there is a spill in the kitchen is to put up a "wet floor" sign to alert others to the hazard. This helps to prevent accidents.

questions.question: A restaurant is located in an area with a history of power outages. What is the best way for the manager to be prepared for a power outage?
answers: Have a backup generator.
Have a large supply of candles and flashlights.
Have a list of other restaurants in the area that have power.
Have a lot of ice on hand to pack in the coolers.
feedbacks: Correct: A backup generator can provide power to the refrigerators and freezers, which is essential for food safety.
Incorrect: While helpful for lighting, this does not address the issue of food safety.
Incorrect: This is not a reliable or safe solution for storing your food.
Incorrect: While ice can help, a generator is a more reliable solution.
questions.explanation: A backup generator is the best way to be prepared for a power outage. It can keep the refrigerators and freezers running, which will prevent the food from spoiling.

questions.question: A food handler has a small, infected cut on their hand. They are wearing a bandage and a single-use glove. When should they change their glove?
answers: Every time they wash their hands.
If the glove becomes torn or ripped.
At least every four hours of continuous use.
Only when they switch to a different task.
At the end of their shift.
When the glove looks dirty.
feedbacks: Correct: A new glove should be put on after handwashing.
Correct: A damaged glove can no longer protect the food from contamination.
Correct: Gloves should be changed regularly, even if they do not appear to be dirty.
Incorrect: Gloves should be changed more frequently than this.
Incorrect: This is too long to wear the same pair of gloves.
Incorrect: A glove can be contaminated even if it does not look dirty.
questions.explanation: Single-use gloves should be changed frequently to prevent the spread of bacteria. This includes after washing hands, if the glove is damaged, and at least every four hours of continuous use.

questions.question: A restaurant is preparing a large batch of chicken soup for a catering order. Which THREE of the following are acceptable methods for cooling the soup?
answers: Placing the pot of soup in the walk-in cooler.
Dividing the soup into smaller, shallow pans and placing them in the walk-in cooler.
Placing the pot of soup in an ice-water bath.
Stirring the soup with an ice paddle.
